Section D. Dues/renewal dues shall be paid annually for the calendar year, January 1 through December 31 and are determined by the executive board. Any increase in dues shall be approved by the general membership. Club membership is required to be renewed annually.

### ARTICLE III - OFFICERS Section A. The executive board is the governing body of the club. It shall consist of (as a minimum) a President, Vice-President, Secretary/Treasurer. Any one member may not hold more than one position on the Executive Board. No two members of the same household may serve on the same executive board. Section B. The Executive Board Members shall be elected by a vote of the general membership, shall serve without compensation and shall be considered the governing body of the Club. The newly elected officers (or appointed officers, in case of a vacancy), shall attest that they have read and understand and will abide by the club’s by-laws, the Association’s Chartered Club Rules and Procedures, and the Schedule of Fees and Community Rules. They do this by signing the New Club Officer’s form CC 50 and forwarding it to the Lifestyle Services by December 1st.

Section C. Terms of Office and Responsibilities Each officer shall serve a term of _____ year(s). The President of the Executive Board is limited to two consecutive terms. Other officers may serve two or more terms, unless otherwise limited by these by-laws. Responsibilities. The president shall preside at all meetings; consult with other officers of the organization and/or the membership on all matters of concern to the organization. The vice-president shall preside at meetings in the absence of the president and assist whenever necessary. The secretary shall record minutes of all executive board meetings and formal meetings of the club’s general membership. The treasurer shall keep all records of financial transactions and assets, collect dues, keep an up-to- date membership list to include the CA# and maintain the club’s checking account. The officers shall each have such powers and duties as generally pertain to their respective offices.

Section D. Nomination and Election Procedures All members of the Executive Board will be elected by the club’s general membership present or electronically. (a) A nominating committee consisting of no less than _____ club members shall be appointed by the ___________ (president or the executive board) at the _________ meeting each year. The nominating committee shall present the proposed slate of officers at the club’s general membership meeting during _________of each year. Nominations may be made from the membership following the report from the nominating committee. (b) Officers shall be elected by a majority vote of the membership. Voting may be by a show of hands if uncontested, electronic or shall be by secret ballot if more than one member is running for the same office.

Section E. Executive Board Meeting Quorum Procedures. The Executive Board shall hold regular meetings and at the discretion of any member of the board. A quorum shall consist of 51% of the executive board members. Section F. Executive Board Meeting Voting Procedures. Voting shall be by majority agreement. Section G. Vacancies of Officers. Interim appointments shall be made by the ____________________ (president or executive board), to fill un-expired terms of office if and when an office becomes vacant. Interim appointment procedures must be followed per club by- laws within 14 days of the vacancy. Section H. Officers (Recall). Written notice of a proposed recall shall be given to members at least two weeks prior to any meeting called for such a purpose. An officer shall be removed from office by a 10% vote of the membership present at such a meeting. The vote shall be by secret ballot.
Section I. All executive board members, upon retiring from office, shall deliver all records, room reservations, historical information and other property belonging to the club to their successor.

### ARTICLE IV - MEMBERSHIP MEETINGS Section A. Types and Frequencies of Meetings. General membership meetings shall be held (e.g., monthly or quarterly). Special meetings may be called by the executive board. All meetings require either written or electronic notice to all members at least two weeks prior to the meeting. An agenda is required to be sent at least one week before the meeting. Section B. Procedures not covered by these by-laws shall be governed by Robert’s Rules of Order. See Appendix C in the CCR&Ps, Parliamentary Procedures. Section C. Quorum. A quorum at a regular or special meeting shall consist of a minimum of 10% of the club’s members at that time. Section D. Voting procedures unless otherwise stated in these by-laws, a majority vote by show of hands, shall be considered the will of the club.

Section E. Intervention Procedure If the Executive Board cannot resolve problems within the board members of the club, then a CC130 shall be sent to Lifestyle Services via email. If an issue arises with the club membership, the club member should bring the issue to the club’s Executive Board. If a problem arises with a member in a sub-group it should be dealt with within the subgroup. If it cannot be dealt with within the subgroup it shall come to the club’s Executive Board.

### ARTICLE V – FINANCIAL Section A. Financial records shall be maintained for a period of seven (7) years. These records shall remain with the current treasurer. Section B. Dual signatures are required on all checks over $500. Electronic payments require two signatures on invoices. All expenditures shall be paid from the club’s checking account, regardless of the amount. The purchasing of all equipment and furniture over five-hundred dollars ($500.00) which is intended to become a permanent asset of the Community Association, must be reviewed and approved by Lifestyles. If the Club has adopted a budget: All activities that involve financial transactions shall operate within the budget which shall be approved annually by the general membership. Non-budgeted

*expenditures of up to $___ per transaction shall be approved by the Treasurer. If the Club does not have a budget: Expenditures of $__________ shall be approved by the treasurer. Expenditures in excess of ____________ shall be approved by two executive board members. Expenditures over $_________ shall be approved by the general membership. Section C. If any financial transactions take place within the club, the records must be certified on an annual basis by an individual(s) other than those elected to the executive board or their immediate family. The results of the certification (i.e., Form CC 90) shall be presented to the general membership and duly recorded in the applicable minutes of the meeting at which presented. If there are special interest or music interest groups, their CC90 must be consolidated into the CC90 of the chartered club.

Section D. Responsibility for cash and inventory control shall be designated to an officer by the executive board. The financial records shall include: - A record of all moneys collected and dispersed into the club’s checking account - An annual membership list (Form CC 20) - An annual inventory of all equipment and furniture on (Form CC 95). - An annual financial report based on a calendar year (Form CC 90). This report shall be submitted to the Lifestyle Services and made available to the general membership.

### ARTICLE VI – COMMITTEES Section A. Standing committees and ad hoc committees shall be created as the executive board deems necessary to promote the objectives of the club. Section B. Committee chairpersons may be appointed by the president or executive board.

### ARTICLE VII – BY-LAW REVISIONS Section A. Notice requirement and procedure. Proposed by-laws changes shall be approved by the executive board and submitted to the Lifestyle Services for preliminary approval prior to their submission to the general membership for its approval. Club members shall be notified in writing of any meeting to amend the by-laws; such notice shall be a minimum of two weeks prior to that meeting. Section B. To revise the by-laws of this club requires a majority vote of the membership present or electronically at a meeting duly called for such a purpose, a quorum being present, and required notice being given. A complete revised copy of the by-laws will be presented to the club members and, upon a majority vote by the membership, will be forwarded to the Lifestyle Director for final approval.

ARTICLE VIII **–** DISSOLUTION Prior to club dissolution, and after all debts are satisfied, all property and assets under the club control shall be documented and physically relinquished to the Community Association through the Lifestyle Services.

## APPENDIX C PARLIAMENTARY PROCEDURES Parliamentary procedures are a set of guidelines for conducting general membership meetings, executive board meetings and committee meetings. These procedures allow everyone to be heard and the group to make decisions by majority rule without confusion. Since these are time tested democratic procedures, they provide order, fairness, decorum and protection for club’s leaders. The following is based upon Robert’s Rules of Order but simplified to be commensurate with the nature of chartered clubs. A. Basic Principles - The group’s president or chair should prepare a preliminary agenda and distribute it in advance of the meeting. - A quorum of 10% of the membership must be present for the group to take action in any meeting. - Only one question at a time may be considered and only one person may have the floor at any one time. - No person can speak until recognized by the chair. - Personal remarks are always out of order.

- No person can speak until recognized by the chair. - Personal remarks are always out of order. - The president or chair should always remain impartial B. Typical Order of Business - Call to Order - Determine if a Quorum is present - Adoption of the Agenda - Reading (may be dispensed with) and approval of the minutes of the previous meeting - Reports of Officers - Reports of Committees - Status of Electronic Ballots - Old Business - New Business - Announcements - Adjournment C. Role of the President or Chair - Set dates and venue for meetings - Remain impartial during debate - Try to develop a consensus – more than a simple majority but NOT necessarily unanimity - Request someone to make a motion, the president or chair does not make motions - Request seconds for motions - Recognize speakers - Maintain order - Put motions to a vote and announce results

- Recognize speakers - Maintain order - Put motions to a vote and announce results - Vote only to break or create a tie – Exception: for elections with more than one person running for the same position ballots shall be used and the president or chair may vote - Initiate electronic letter ballots for the Executive Board D. Procedure for Handling Motions - Member makes a motion - Motion seconded by a different member (if no second the motion is dead) - Any member can suggest a modification of the wording to clarify the motion. The maker of the motion can choose to accept or reject the modified wording (does not require a second) - The president or chair will restate the motion and open debate. - After the debate ends or a reasonable time has been allowed for debate; if necessary, the president or chair clarifies the consequences of affirmative and negative vote

- The president or chair calls for a vote by a show of hands and announces the result. The president or chair does not vote except to break or create a tie. If there is a tie the motion fails. E. Electronic Letter Ballots - Electronic Letter Ballots should include: a) Title b) Statement; an explanation of the issue or project c) Question; exactly what is being voted on d) I vote; agree, disagree, abstain e) Voters name f) Due date and time - If during the balloting a single person votes “Disagree” the balloting stops and must wait for the next face-to-face meeting so the matter can be discussed. F. EXECUTIVE BOARD MEETING VOTING PROCEDURES - Executive board members may participate by telephonic or electronic means in meetings and possess the same authority as members who are physically present at the meeting, provided that all of the following conditions are met: 1. The presiding officer/chairman and two (2) other executive board members are physically present at the meeting place

2. All members attending in person or by telephonic or electronic means can hear any and all comments made at the meeting 3. All comments, motions, and votes of the member(s) attending by electronic means are recorded in the minutes of the meeting 4. Voting shall be by majority agreement Electronic participation shall be limited to situations that prevent physical attendance at the meeting.

# Chartered Clubs and Registered Community Groups Living in Sun City Hilton Head is all about embracing the lifestyle this community offers, which includes a lively, robust and exciting social scene constantly buzzing with activity. Sun City’s Chartered Clubs and Registered Community Groups provide residents with endless ways to meet friends, play sports, get creative, give back to the greater community and so much more. With more than 100 options, there is sure to be a Chartered Club or Registered Community Group that caters to every interest or hobby. From casual card games to gardening, stamp collecting to line dancing, sports to philanthropic organizations, it can all be found within these pages.

Now in its fifth year, the Club Catalog has become a popular resource for newcomers and long-time residents when navigating the club and group options. While every issue of *SunSations* magazine contains a Chartered Club and Registered Community Group News Directory, the Club Catalog is meant to provide useful and more in-depth information for each club and group in one publication. This edition includes the most up-to-date directory of Sun City’s clubs and groups, as well as officer contact information, instructions on how to join or renew membership, and organization descriptions. Viewing this publication online allows you to hover and click on the links to navigate directly to the club and group webpages for even more information. Turn to the back of this issue to find additional resources and information pertaining to clubs and groups in Sun City, including how to receive the twice-monthly Clubs and Groups eNewsletter and how to establish a new club or group.

Be sure to download this issue to your computer or print it at home and keep it handy to reference year-round. We hope everyone finds something in these pages to help you fulfill your active adult lifestyle. As Sun City celebrates its 30th anniversary this year, there is sure to be even more fun ahead! For more information about clubs and groups, please contact Lifestyle Services at (843) 705-4027.

## Additional Resources and Information ### How to Sign Up for the Clubs and Groups eNewsletter Keep track of Sun City's club and group community-wide events with the twice-monthly Clubs and Groups eNewsletter! Delivered to subscribers on the second and fourth Wednesday of the month, this eNewsletter includes an overview of the upcoming Chartered Club and Registered Community Group events that are open to all Sun City residents. Residents must be subscribed to eNews Weekly to receive the newsletter. #### Signing up is easy! 1. Log into [www.SunCityHiltonHead.org](https://www.SunCityHiltonHead.org). 2. From Resident Central, scroll to the Account Management tile and click "Opt-In eNewsletters." 3. Fill out the form. To receive the Clubs and Groups eNewsletter, check that option at the bottom of the form. 4. Click "Subscribe." ##### Current eNews Subscribers

4. Click "Subscribe." ##### Current eNews Subscribers If you currently receive eNews Weekly but do not receive the Clubs and Groups eNewsletter, please see below for opt-in instructions: - Scroll to the bottom of any eNews Weekly or The Week Ahead email and click the "Update Your Preferences" link. - Click "Email Me a Link" on the next window. - You will receive an email with a link to update your subscriptions. Click "Update Your Preferences" in the email. - Select the Clubs and Groups eNewsletter. Then click "Update Profile." ---

### How to Submit Information for the Clubs and Groups eNewsletter The Clubs and Groups eNewsletter is published on the second and fourth Wednesday of each month. The deadline for inclusion is noon on the Monday prior to publication. Email [communications@schhca.com](mailto:communications@schhca.com) with event details in the body of the email or as a Microsoft Word attachment. #### Submission Guidelines - Clubs and groups may promote four different events per year in the Clubs and Groups eNewsletter. - Each of the four events may be promoted twice in the two issues of the eNewsletter prior to the event. - Events must be open to all residents and held inside Sun City. - Submissions should be no more than 100 words. - Any Special Interest Group wanting to use one of the four events must obtain written approval from its parent club. - Submissions cannot solicit members.

### Explore the Club and Group Webpages Every Chartered Club and Registered Community Group has its own webpage at [www.SunCityHiltonHead.org](https://www.SunCityHiltonHead.org). #### To find club and group webpages: - Log into [www.SunCityHiltonHead.org](https://www.SunCityHiltonHead.org). - From Resident Central, scroll to the Clubs & Groups tile and click "Learn More." - Scroll down to find a club based on its category. - Clubs are organized by category as they are listed in this catalog, including cards & games, hobbies, general interest, performing arts, and sports. - Click "Registered Community Groups" for an alphabetical list of groups. ---

### Editing Your Club or Group’s Webpage Club and group webpage administrators can update and edit club and group webpages on [www.SunCityHiltonHead.org](https://www.SunCityHiltonHead.org). #### To find tutorials about editing webpages: - Visit [www.SunCityHiltonHead.org](https://www.SunCityHiltonHead.org). - Click the "FAQs" button at the top of the page. - In the Table of Contents, look for the Tutorials section and click "Website Editing Tutorials for Clubs, Groups, Neighborhoods and BACs." For questions about your club or group's webpage editing permissions, please call Lifestyle Services at (843) 705-4027. ---

### Establishing a New Chartered Club or Registered Community Group Are you interested in starting a new Chartered Club or Registered Community Group? Be sure to contact the Lifestyle Services Department at (843) 705-4027 for all the information you need to get started. Staff will guide you through the steps of establishing your organization. Here is some helpful information: #### Chartered Clubs - Must maintain a roster of 100 or more active Sun City residents. - Only Sun City residents can become members. - Are allowed to require members to pay dues to generate revenue. - May not set certain preconditions for membership or be tied to vocations, religion, politics, specific geological regions, etc. #### Registered Community Groups - May include non-resident members, but the total membership must be two-thirds, or 67 percent, Sun City residents, with at least 40 members total. - May be formed based on social, service, political, geographical, vocational, or educational interests.

- May only have Sun City residents acting as board members. #### Clubs or Groups in Formation Clubs or groups that are not yet established and looking to secure membership may contact Lifestyle Services first. At the direction of Lifestyle Services, the organization may be listed as a club or group in formation in the Club or Group News section of *SunSations*. The word limit for groups in formation is 25 words, and they may be listed in the magazine for up to three consecutive months.

# Managed Neighborhoods Sun City North & Sun City West Package Several aspects of your landscape maintenance are provided to you by the Sun City Hilton Head Community Association through your benefit assessment fees. The Managed Neighborhoods Office manages and works in partnership with BrightView to assure delivery of these services as outlined in the landscape maintenance scope of work. Please keep in mind that the information in this packet is an outline of the included services, however, due to weather conditions, holidays or other unforeseen circumstances, some aspects of these services may change relative to frequency or when the service is provided. If you have questions, comments or concerns regarding your benefitted landscape services, please contact the Managed Neighborhoods Office at managed.neighborhoods@schhca.com or call (843) 705-4061; be sure to include your name, address, contact information and issue or concern.

## Sun City North Managed Neighborhoods: Botany Bay Carolina Landings Cedar Run Edgewater Foxlake Greenbriar Park Heron’s Pointe Juniper Creek Magnolia Crossing Mariner’s Cove Marsh Cove Northlake Oak Terrace Rivergrass Sanctuary Cove Serenity Walk Turnberry Woods Village Green Whispering Oaks Wildlife Bay

## Submitting a Work Order Ticket The Community Association utilizes a work ticket system for residents to submit issues pertaining to various departments such as Common Area, Facilities Maintenance and Managed Neighborhoods (MN). Relative to Managed Neighborhoods, please read below for information on what types of issues should be submitted through the work ticket system and which should not.

### Work Order Ticket Required Please email WebHelpDesk@schhca.com to submit a work ticket with your name, phone number, your address, and the issue or concern; please attach a photo(s) to your email** as they are very helpful. Once you submit your work ticket, you’ll receive a confirmation email from the work ticket system with “[Ticket #XXXXX]” in the subject line. Please make note of the work ticket number (WT#). If you have questions or additional information to add, please reply to any email that you receive from the work ticket system that has the matching WT#. Doing so will apply your correspondence directly to the work ticket keeping all pertinent information together. You will continue to receive emails from the work ticket system anytime a note is added to your work ticket until it has been closed.

### As Needed Services We heavily rely on a good partnership with our residents to inform us if they require an “as needed” service(s) by submitting a work ticket as each property is unique and has slightly different needs. Examples of “as needed” services: developer plant bed weed control, crack weeds, or turf condition issues (discoloration, dying, thinning, possible fungus or insects, etc.).

### Missed Service Once it has been communicated via the Daily Update email that all services have been completed in your neighborhood*, residents may submit a work order ticket to the system informing us that your property did not receive complete services. Please ensure that you only do this AFTER reviewing the Daily Update email, as sometimes there are instances where weather or turf conditions will force the vendor to skip over specific aspects of service. Examples of missed services: grass clippings left on** patios, one side of the driveway being edged but not the other, back yard mowed, but not the front yard, etc. _*Please note that any work tickets generated prior to the Daily Update email stating that an entire neighborhood has been_ _completed will be closed._

### Damage Any damage sustained during services provided as a part of your Sun City North & Sun City West Package should be submitted through the work ticket system. Some examples of this are: turf scalping, home or property damage caused during service, chemical burn, tire ruts**, etc.

### Items that should not be submitted to the work ticket system Items that are not included in the Sun City North & Sun City West Package should not be submitted to the work ticket system as they are a resident responsibility. Examples of these items are as follows: - Drainage issues or standing water - Animal pest issues - General questions (please direct general questions regarding MN to Managed Neighborhoods@schhca.com) - Irrigation system problems or maintenance requests (unless damage was caused by the Association’s vendor) - Turf issues (lumpy turf) or turf decline due to drainage issues, previous fungus damage, root intrusion, shade, over-irrigation, etc. (unless damage was caused by the Association’s vendor) - Tracks, not ruts, left by mowers** - Tree, shrub, or other planting concerns (including the re-staking of a tree) - Issues regarding landscape materials installed by Pulte

- Issues regarding landscape materials installed by Pulte - Proposal requests for out of contract services, or any issues pertaining to additional services that you have privately contracted with our vendor _Ruts and tracks are often confused. Ruts refer to deep depressions into (typically) oversaturated turf/soil leaving a clear,_ _defined, impression of a tire (tread and outer edges of the tire), sometimes several inches, into the ground. Ruts typically_ _need some sort of intervention to repair whether tamping the earth down or replacement of the sod. Tracks are superficial marks left by tires in moist soil/turf where markings of the treads of a tire are present but lack a deep, clear impression of the outer edges of a tire._

## Landscape Maintenance **The Sun City North & Sun City West Package includes the following items:** Weekly lawn mowing (weather permitting) during the growing season (April – October), as needed services are provided the remainder of the year as deemed necessary by SCHHCA Managed Neighborhoods. Edging around walkways, driveways and developer planting beds*, no less than every other visit, depending on conditions. Clippings blown from walkways, driveways and porches/patios (not enclosed) at each mowing service. Weed control of plant beds* (as needed.) Up to six turf applications per year to include fertilizations, pre-emergent and insecticide. Post-emergent spread throughout the program as needed. One fungicide application, if necessary. Two pine straw applications per year, spring and fall, which includes developer plant beds* only. One irrigation system inspection per year (winter/early spring) to review the overall function of your system.

a. A door tag will be left at each residence denoting any issue(s) found in need of repair. b. Only minor adjustments such as a broken head replacement will be made to the irrigation system (as a courtesy), as irrigation maintenance is a resident responsibility. _All repairs are optional. Residents may contact the vendor directly to schedule any needed repair(s) using the contact information listed on the door tag, or they may contact another vendor of their choice._ Residents can opt out of select services only and must do so during the opt out window which takes place prior to the season starting (November-December). Flags will be delivered to your home by the landscape provider prior to the first application or service. **Red – Denotes no turf applications** **Blue - Denotes no irrigation system inspection**

**Red – Denotes no turf applications** **Blue - Denotes no irrigation system inspection** Flags denoting opt-outs will be placed in the yard and must remain where they are placed to ensure visibility. Red flags must remain the entire season. Blue flags can be removed once the service has concluded in the entire neighborhood. There is no reduction in costs or materials for residents who voluntarily opt-out of service(s). Opt-out provisions exclusively apply to turf applications, irrigation system and pine straw applications. Residents may not opt-out of the fungicide and insecticide applications as an infestation may directly affect the entire neighborhood or community. _Developer (installed) plant beds refers to the front planting bed at the foundation of the home, utility plant beds and front yard tree ring._

### Service Schedule During the growing season, the Managed Neighborhoods Office sends the NRs & ANRs a daily update email which includes detailed information, for them to share with their neighbors, regarding the current service schedule. During the dormant season, pertinent updates are shared via email with NRs & ANRs, as necessary, who will then distribute these service updates to their neighbors. A condensed version of the same information provided to the NRs/ANRs will also be posted to the Buzz Line at (843) 645-4517. The recording is updated each weekday, Monday-Friday.

## Turf Application Schedule ### Agronomic Program Details: Bermuda and Centipede #### February/March (application 1): - Granular pre-emergent application and “Poly-On” polymer coated slow-release fertilizer (activated when surface temperature reaches 55 degrees, continuous feed through August) - Fertilizer ratio 3-1-2 (based on current conditions prior to application) - Nitrogen application is based on conditions annually #### April/May (applications 2 and 3): - Insecticide application targeting mole crickets and fire ants (12 month residual effect) - Post emergent herbicide application (grassy and broadleaf weed control) #### June/July (application 4): - Post emergent herbicide application (grassy and broadleaf weed control) - Iron application (as needed) #### August/September (application 5): - Post emergent herbicide application (grassy and broadleaf weed control) - Iron application (as needed) - Insecticide application for army worm activity (as needed)

- Iron application (as needed) - Insecticide application for army worm activity (as needed) #### October (application 6): - Granular pre-emergent application (to prevent weed growth the following season) - Fungicide application (as needed) Our vendor will use its best judgement when scheduling turf applications to minimize any potential dilution due to weather. As outlined above, dependent on various factors including timing, conditions, efficiency, or other reasons, the landscape provider may combine certain applications when applicable. The application schedule, products and methods of application may change due to conditions, temperatures, resistance and current needs of the turf species. The current program will help control weeds but cannot eliminate them entirely.

## Mandatory Applications ### Insecticide Fipronil, referred to as Top Choice, is a systemic and contact insecticide which will be applied as warranted throughout the entire community. This product will target specific pests that damage turf such as: mole crickets, army worms and fire ants. The timeliness of the application will be at the suggestion of the contractor. Additional applications of insecticides may be necessary throughout the growing season.

### Fungicide A fungicide (product TBD) with systemic and contact qualities will be applied to contain fungus and provide a 21-28-day residual. This is a one-time application covered under the contract. If additional applications are required, it will be at the expense of the homeowner. BrightView can provide additional applications upon requests through their office. BrightView will only apply this product if there are signs of fungus emerging “naturally” throughout the community. The targeted fungus is “brown patch.” If necessary, communication will be sent ahead of time as to the date of the application. **Dates will be provided prior to each application. Products may vary due to weather conditions. The turf application schedule is weather dependent and permitting.**

## Irrigation Repairs All aspects of irrigation systems, including adjustments and programming, are the responsibility of the homeowner and not included under maintenance. To request repair services, please contact BrightView directly at suncityhhwt@brightview.com. Residents may also hire an outside irrigation contractor of their choice. BrightView will accept responsibility for damages caused to irrigation systems during lawn care services by submitting a work order ticket as outlined previously in this package.

# Couples Golf Format Descriptions > ALL SCORES ARE POSTED TO GHIN BY GOLF GENIUS UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED ALWAYS RECORD GROSS SCORES - GOLF GENIUS CALCULATES NET SCORES

## ONE BEST GROSS AND ONE BEST NET This is a 4 person event. All players play their own ball and record gross scores. The team score adds together one best gross score and one best net score of the foursome. The low gross and low net cannot be counted from the same person. If the gross score is counted, the next low net will be used for the team score. This event is flighted and handicapped at 100%

## BEST NET OF A/C and BEST NET OF B/D This is a 4 person event. The low index player in couple #1 is the A player and their partner is B. The low index player in couple #2 is the C player and their partner is D. All players play their won ball and record gross scores. Scoring counts the one best net of player A & C added to the one best net of player B & D This event is flighted and handicapped at 100%

## ODD/EVEN – 3 NET ON ODD HOLES AND 2 NET ON EVEN HOLES This is a 4 person event. All players play their own ball and record gross scores. The team score adds together the 3 best net scores on odd holes, and 2 best net scores on even holes. This event flighted and handicapped at 100%

## STEP ASIDE SCRAMBLE This is a 4 person event. All players tee off. The team decides which tee shot to use. The person whose ball is chosen “steps aside” and doesn’t play the next shot. The process is repeated on each shot through the hole until the ball is in the hole. Three players hit each shot with the person who played the previous shot sitting out. You may move the ball up to one club length from where the selected ball lies, no closer to the hole, staying in the same condition (fairway stays in fairway, rough stays in rough, and penalty stays in the penalty area). This event is flighted only – scores are not posted.

## STABLEFORD SCORING – COUNT TWO BEST STABLEFORD SCORES This is a 4 person event. All players play their own ball and record gross scores. Stableford points are awarded to each NET score as follows: NET BOGIE – 1 POINT NET PAR – 2 POINTS NET BIRDIE – 4 POINTS NET EAGLE – 6 POINTS In this event, high scores win. The two highest stableford points are added together for the team score. If a score exceeds NET BOGIE, pick up the ball because no Stableford points will be awarded. Record the expected gross score for this player. This event is flighted and handicapped at 100%

# COUPLE SCRAMBLE This is a two person event Both players tee off. Select the best drive and then both players hit a ball from that spot. Then select the best ball from those two results and both players hit the next shot from there. Keep repeating, both players hitting, including on the green, until the ball is in the hole. You may move the ball up to one club length from where it lies, no closer to the hole and in the same condition (fairway stays in fairway, rough stays in rough, hazard stays in hazard). This event is flighted only - scores are not posted

## 3 BEST NET OF 4 This is a 4 person event. All players play their own ball and record gross scores. The 3 best net scores are added together for the team score. This event is flighted and handicapped at 100%

## SHAMBLE This is a 4 person event. All players tee off and select one drive. From that point everyone plays their own ball through the green. (there are always 4 balls in play). Record the gross score for each player. The selected tee shot may be moved one club length from where it lies, no closer to the hole, staying in the same condition (fairway stays in fairway, rough stays in rough, and hazard stays in hazard) This event is flighted and handicapped at 100% - scores are not posted

## I NET ON PAR 5s, 2 NETS ON PAR 4s, 3 NETS ON PAR 3s This is a 4 person event. All players play their own ball and record gross scores. Team score counts one best net score on par 5s, two best net scores on par 4s, and 3 best net scores on par 3s This event is flighted and handicapped at 100%

## BEST NET OF COUPLE This is a two person event. Each person in the pair plays their own ball and records gross score. The team score is the one best net score of the couple. This event is flighted and handicapped at 100%

## COMBINED NET SCORE This is a two person event. Each player plays their own ball and gross scores are recorded. The team score is the combined net of the twosome. This flight is handicapped and flighted at 100%

## 3,3,3 and 6,6,6 These are two person events where three different formats are played – scramble, best ball, and alternate shot. In a 9 hole event: Play the first 3 holes in a couple scramble (recording one score for the team) Play the second 3 holes as best ball - each play your own ball and record your gross score (best net score counts) Play the last 3 holes as modified alternate shot (recording one score for the team). In an 18 hole event, the same formats will be followed, but you will play 6 holes of each. - Scramble – both players tee off. Then select the best drive and both players hit from that spot. Then select the best ball from that outcome and both play from that spot. Keep repeating, both players hitting until the ball is holed out. Once a ball is selected to play, you may move it within one club length, no closer to the hole, in the same condition.

- Best ball – both players play their own ball all the way through the hole and record gross scores. The best net of the couple counts as the team score. - Modified alternate shot – Both players tee off, select the best ball and alternate shots from there, beginning with the person who did not hit the tee shot. The ball selected must be played throughout the hole – no switching balls. This event is flighted and only the best ball section is handicapped. Scores are not posted

## MODIFIED ALTERNATE SHOT Both players tee off and select the best ball. Alternate shots from there, beginning with the person who did not hit the tee shot. The ball selected must be played throughout the hole – no switching balls. On the next hole, start the process again with both teeing off and then alternating shots from the selected bll. This event is flighted only - Scores are not posted

## MODIFIED BEST BALL Both players tee off, then switch and play each other’s tee shot. Continue to play that ball throughout the hole. The team score is the best net score of the couple. You must play the ball hit from the tee box, no switching balls. If a player hits a tee shot that results in a penalty stroke, the partner who plays the ball in takes that penalty. This event is flighted and handicapped 100% Scores are not posted.

# Sun City Hilton Head Villa Owner’s Manual **Developed jointly by Management and Villa Neighborhood Representatives** **September 2015 Welcome Letter From The Board of Directors** Dear Villa Owner: We are delighted that you have chosen to purchase a Villa in Sun City Hilton Head, the biggest active adult community in the Lowcountry. As one of the 635 Villa owners, you have certain benefits and certain responsibilities that are outlined in this manual. These benefits and responsibilities are all defined in your neighborhood’s Supplemental Declarations, which, along with other governing documents, define the duties of the owner (you) and the Community Association. You will find your neighborhood’s Supplemental Declaration and other related documents in the Appendices of this manual.

This manual was developed with you in mind and is the result of a recommendation from the 20132014 Villa Task Force. This Task Force, comprised of association management staff and resident volunteers, was appointed by the Board of Directors in 2013 to review some of the concerns and challenges that villa owners face and recommend best practices to maximize lifestyle enjoyment in these neighborhoods. This manual outlining the unique aspects of Villa ownership was a part of the Task Force’s recommendation. It was completed in a collaborative effort between Management and Villa Neighborhood Representatives. Keep this manual close at hand in your home; it is a valuable reference and can answer many questions you may have. Enjoy the Lifestyle, Sun City Hilton Head Board of Directors Last revised April 2019 ----- **Welcome Letter From Your Neighborhood Representative** Dear Villa Owner:

----- **Welcome Letter From Your Neighborhood Representative** Dear Villa Owner: We want to join the Board of Directors in providing an introduction to your Villa Owner’s Manual. Working with Association Management, we have included helpful information and divided it into the following sections: **1.** **Overview of Villa Ownership** - Provides an important description of the ownership and management of your Villa - Explains terminology used throughout the manual **2.** **Financial Information** - Provides insight into how budgets and Villa assessments are established - Explains tracking of expenses compared to the budget - Describes the treatment of Reserve Funds **3.** **Insurance** - Explains coverage on your Villa provided by the Community Association and describes insurance policies that you should carry - Outlines the process for filing a claim for an insured loss **4.** **Landscaping**

- Outlines the process for filing a claim for an insured loss **4.** **Landscaping** - Describes the landscaping service provided by the Community Association and the flexibility you have regarding landscaping **5.** **Maintenance and Additions** - Describes, in detail, the services funded by your assessments and the other services you are responsible for - Outlines the process for making changes or additions to your Villa **6.** **FAQs** - In addition to the FAQs included at the end of each section, this section provides answers to frequently asked questions that do not fall under a specific section **7.** **Neighborhood** - Use this tabbed section of your manual to store information specific to your neighborhood; this information is provided by your Neighborhood Representative

We are providing this manual in this loose-leaf format so that changes or additions can be made as necessary. If you have any questions, you can contact either of us or the Managed Neighborhoods Office. Finally, please provide your feedback so we can gauge if this effort has been worthwhile and what might be helpful in future updates. ## Overview of Villa Ownership Your Villa ownership includes benefits provided to you as a result of the assessments you pay. This overview of Villa Ownership provides the information you need to enjoy your Villa by understanding just how the benefits are managed, and how you can influence that management.

### Sun City Hilton Head Structure Your Villa is part of Sun City Hilton Head (Sun City) and a part of the Sun City Hilton Head Community Association. Some of your ownership benefits and responsibilities are by virtue of being within Sun City. Although those benefits and responsibilities will not be covered in detail, a few important highlights are below. Before covering those points, there are four information sources you can use to find additional information about what is going on in Sun City: 1. **_SunSations_:** Monthly magazine delivered to your mailbox._ 2. **Community Website www.SunCityHiltonHead.org:** Resident-only section available with login** credentials. Click on “Member Login” to get started. First-time users can click on a link on the login page to get set up.

3. **Electronic Newsletters:** Our Communications Department sends out eNews Weekly, the Week Ahead, BOD Updates, the Neighborhood Newsletter and other specialty electronic communications to residents who have opted in to receive them. Neighborhoods may also have their own email newsletters; check with your Neighborhood Representative. 4. **Open Meetings:** Most meetings of the Board of Directors, Board Appointed Committees and other organizational bodies are open to Sun City residents. In addition, there are specific meetings intended for the membership, which you are encouraged to attend. #### PulteGroup - Developer of Sun City Hilton Head

#### PulteGroup - Developer of Sun City Hilton Head PulteGroup, the developer of Sun City Hilton Head, builds and sells homes in Sun City. Pulte appointees to the Board of Directors make up a majority of the Board. Pulte is not involved in the day-to-day operations of the Community Association beyond its continued development of new lots and streets. Pulte is no longer building or selling Villas, and has no plans to do so in the future. Other than warranties that may exist for owners of some Villas, PulteGroup has no financial involvement with the Villa Neighborhoods. The previous paragraph is a brief description of the Developer’s involvement with the Community Association. In addition, the Developer has significant latitude in their ability to change the Governing Documents described below. The Association Board of Directors can recommend changes to the developer based on the needs of the community. #### Board of Directors

#### Board of Directors Sun City Hilton Head Community Association has a Board of Directors that sets the policies for the Association. The Board is comprised of three members appointed by PulteGroup, two elected residents, and two non-voting resident alternates. Contact information is listed in SunSations magazine. #### Association Management Company The Board has contracted with a management company to manage the day-to-day operations of the Community Association. The company specializes in management of Lifestyle and Active Adult Communities. When you go to the administrative center in Palmetto Commons, when you get fitness help at one of the Fitness Centers, or when you deal with any staff member throughout the community, you are dealing with an association management employee. Contact information for employees can be found in SunSations. #### Governing Documents

#### Governing Documents Sun City is a non-profit corporation with a number of Governing Documents that provide both the legal foundation for ownership within Sun City, as well as the operational foundation for actions taken by the Community Association. In order of their legal precedence, the Governing Documents are listed below. Although a brief description of each document is provided, the official wording can be found in the documents themselves and those documents are the authority on which the management of your neighborhood is based. Except where noted, these documents are viewable by logging into **www.SunCityHiltonHead.org, clicking on “Documents” under the Community Library tile and then** clicking “Governing Documents.” 1. **Recorded Plats and Deeds:** Shows the precise location of each lot and the “Exclusive Common Areas.” It also defines the owner’s and the community’s title to the property.

2. **The Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (CC&Rs):** These are part of your deed to your Villa as it is registered in Beaufort County. These were created at the inception of Sun City and are only rarely modified. They can be only modified by the Developer (PulteGroup). However, the Board of Directors can recommend a change to the Developer. 3. **Supplemental Declarations:** These documents are supplements to the CC&Rs for each individual Villa neighborhood that describe specific responsibilities of the Developer, the Association, and the Villa owners related to each neighborhood. They also describe which lots are included in the Neighborhood. In the Appendices, you will find the Supplemental Declaration for your neighborhood and an Amendment to that Supplement. A Neighborhood may request that the Board consider a specific change to their Supplemental Declaration. 4. **Articles of Incorporation:** This document provides the legal description of the Sun City Hilton

Head Corporation. 5. **Bylaws:** This document defines how Sun City Hilton Head operates. They can be amended by the Developer or by the Board with the agreement of the Developer. 6. **Board Policies:** These are issued by the Board to establish an operating policy for something not covered by the above documents. Between Sun City’s incorporation in 1995 and February 2015, the Board has issued 179 policies. As an example, Policy 1401.1 concerns the cleaning of Villa Gutters that you will read about in the Maintenance Section.

7. **Design Guidelines:** The Design Guidelines were established to maintain the integrity of the architectural and design characteristics of Sun City Hilton Head. They describe what changes are permitted to the exterior of a property for all residences in Sun City, including Houses, Cottages and Villas. There are Design Guidelines that are specific to Villas, and these are provided in the Appendices. The Design Guidelines can be changed by the Board of Directors, and the Modifications Committee can recommend changes to the Board. Any new provisions cannot be applied retroactively. 8. **Community Rules:** These are the operating rules provided by the Board to association management, which implements the rules through operating procedures they create. As an example, there are rules as to how many activity cards an owner may have under various situations. There are no Community Rules specific to owners of Villas, but you must still abide by the Rules as a member of Sun City.

You will see how these documents come into play as you read the remainder of this manual. #### Community Standards Collectively, the Governing Documents described above are referred to as the Community Standards and are administered by the Community Standards Department on behalf of the Community Association. If you wanted to make an exterior modification to your home, you would fill out an application describing what you would like to do along with required documentation and submit it to the Community Standards Department. If your modification request meets the requirements of the Governing Documents, primarily the Design Guidelines in this case, it would be approved by the Modifications Committee and you could proceed. Administering the Community Standards in a consistent way throughout Sun City plays a major role in maintaining the beauty and property values of the community. #### Neighborhood Representative Council

#### Neighborhood Representative Council Sun City has approximately 50 different Neighborhoods, including seven Villa Neighborhoods. The Neighborhood Representative Council (NRC), comprised of representatives from the Neighborhoods, meets monthly as an information conduit back and forth between owners in the Neighborhoods, the Board and the Association. The Neighborhoods are also assigned to a District of the NRC. The seven Villa Neighborhoods comprise District 2. Neighborhood Representatives in District 2 meet monthly or as needed to provide a voice for specific interests of the Villa Neighborhoods.

## Villa Neighborhoods The Villa Neighborhoods with the number of Villas in each are as follows: - Coastal Villas (81 units) - Egret Cove (59 units) - Live Oak Village (164 units; includes Ansley Place Villas) - The Aviary (83 units) - The Preserve (122 units) - Seaford Place (64 units) - Summerplace Village (62 units)

### Villa Neighborhood Representatives Each Neighborhood elects a Neighborhood Representative (NR) and an Alternate Neighborhood Representative (ANR). The Neighborhood Representatives play a valuable role for owners, including: - They monitor the financial position of the Neighborhood and participate in the annual Neighborhood budget process. - They conduct at least one Neighborhood meeting annually to review the financial standing of the Neighborhood. - They receive notice of all Work Tickets related to the Neighborhood and submit Service Requests needed for neighborhood-wide issues. - They strive to attend the monthly NRC meetings, passing information in both directions. - They are available to discuss broader concerns and raise issues at the NRC meeting if appropriate. - They maintain the subscriptions to the email list server for Neighborhood communications and the Neighborhood website in the Community Groups portion of the Sun City website.
If you have a question that relates to your Villa Neighborhood that you cannot resolve on your own, you may contact your Neighborhood Representative for assistance.

### Neighborhood Social Events Many Neighborhoods have a Social Committee or other group to coordinate social functions for the owners. If you would like to help out or lead an event, contact your Social Chairperson or one of your representatives. The Social Committee typically has a checking account that can be used for decorating neighborhood signs, pre-paying expenses for Neighborhood social functions and the like. This account is not connected with your Assessments, and the transactions are summarized and reported to the NRC annually. The initial funding of this account comes from an informal process within each Neighborhood.

## Paying for Sun City Benefits The many amenities, benefits and services provided by Sun City are paid for through Assessments. Villa owners pay the base HOA assessment and its neighborhood-specific Villa assessment. There are two portions to each Assessment: Operating Assessment covers the cost of operating the facilities and capital expenditures; Reserve Assessment is set aside to defray the future cost of replacing, repairing or restoring a Reserve Component that the Association is obligated to maintain to its original functional condition. More information on assessments is covered in the Financial Information section of this manual.

## Villa Neighborhood Management Each Villa Neighborhood is a “Managed Neighborhood.” The Supplemental Declarations to the CC&Rs as shown in the Appendices define exactly what that means, and Villa owners should read the document. In summary, the elements of being a Managed Neighborhood include the following:

### Grounds and Landscaping Overview 1. In addition to your Villa, you own the plot of ground that is described on your deed. Your use of that space is subject to the documents described above, which are part of your deed. 2. Additionally, the collective space that surrounds the Villas, including the space between the Villas, is defined as the Exclusive Common Area of your Neighborhood. This can be seen in the plat in the Appendices. The Neighborhood Exclusive Common Areas are different from other Community Association the Common Areas, which include amenities and open spaces. 3. The Association Management Company, through the Manager of Managed Neighborhoods, is responsible for the maintenance of all Villa Neighborhood landscaping, including the Exclusive Common Area. The maintenance is subcontracted to a landscape maintenance contractor.

4. In general, you may not maintain the landscaping in any way. However, you may request to replace your shrubbery with approved plant material by submitting a Modifications Application to the Community Standards Department or the Managed Neighborhood Office. 5. You may have ornamentation (flower pots, decorative items, etc.). The rules for Villas are basically the same as for houses concerning with the additional provision that any ornamentation is one foot from any grass. This subject is covered in greater detail in the Landscaping Section.

### Exterior Maintenance Overview 1. Any changes to the exterior of your home must meet the requirements of the Design Guidelines and must be pre-approved by the Community Standards Department. 2. You are responsible for maintaining your driveway, sidewalks, windows, doors (including garage door) and exterior facade. 3. You are not responsible for the irrigation system unless you damage it. 4. You are not responsible for your roof unless you damage or alter it. 5. You may apply pest control treatments around your Villa or hire a service to do that for you. This subject is covered in greater detail in the Maintenance Section.

### Interior Maintenance Overview 1. You are responsible for everything inside the Villa: all plumbing, heating, electrical, air conditioning, floor coverings, walls, smoke alarms and anything else inside. 2. No approvals or applications are required for changes made inside your Villa, but changes must comply with city/county zoning and permit requirements. This subject is covered in greater detail in the Maintenance Section.

### Service Requests If you have an issue with landscaping (such as fire ants, an irrigation failure or a dead bush) or a roof maintenance problem (such as missing shingles), you should contact the Managed Neighborhoods Office via email at managed.neighborhoods@schhca.com (include your name, address and activity card number) or (843) 645-4517. Office staff will assess the situation, determine the responsible party and issue a Work Order Ticket if necessary to correct the problem. Service Requests are to be submitted by the owner of the Villa, not by a tenant.

### Insurance Overview 1. The Association provides structural insurance, which includes wind, hail, fire, earthquake and flood coverage on your Villa as originally built. 2. An HO-6 (condominium/renters) insurance policy is recommended for the contents of your Villa and any improvements/additions you made, as well as for your personal liability. 3. You can also purchase a flood policy for contents and those items beyond the originally built structure from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) through your insurance agent. 4. Other than for flood damage, any deductible for losses covered under Association-provided insurance policies are shared among all Villa Owners as described in Board Policy 0807.3 that can be found in the Appendices. The Flood Policy is a per-building policy, so any loss deductible is shared among the building unit owners. This subject is covered in greater detail in the Insurance Section.

### Financial Management Overview Similar to the Sun City base assessments, there are two additional assessments specifically for each Villa Neighborhood: Operating and Reserve. - **The Operating Assessment** is determined during the budgeting process that involves the Neighborhood Representative on a few of the items. Insurance and Landscape Services comprise more than 80 percent of the budget. About 5 percent of the budget is for landscaping needs like drainage problems. The Neighborhood can decide to provide more money for things like special landscaping projects. - **The Reserve Assessment** is set based on a Reserve Study conducted by a third party to provide the best estimate of the funds that will be needed in the future for the replacement of the roofs and painting/staining/sealing the exterior of the Villas (stucco or other material).

It is important to note that all money spent on behalf of the Neighborhood comes from the Villa assessment that owners pay each year. In most cases, the spending is covered by a line item in the current year’s budget and assessment.

### Villa Warranty In general, most warranties from the builder have expired. If there is remaining warranty on an item in your Villa, the matter is strictly between you and PulteGroup, and does not involve the Neighborhood or the Association. Warranty issues should be handled according to the warranty documents provided at the time your Villa was purchased from the PulteGroup. If in doubt, send an email to hiltonheadservice@delwebb.com.

## Frequently Asked Questions about Villa Ownership 1. **Can I rent out my Villa?** You may rent out your Villa in the same manner and with the same restrictions as owners of any home in Sun City Hilton Head. The minimum term for any rental is 90 days. In order for your tenants to obtain an activity card and a bar code for their vehicles, you must surrender your own activity card during the term of the lease. ## Financial Information As covered in the Overview of Villa Ownership, you pay two assessments related to the Villa Neighborhood, namely, the restricted Reserve Assessment and the general Operating Assessment. These are described in detail below. While procedurally the Villa Assessment is paid to the Sun City Community Association, these neighborhood assessments are separate and distinct from the association assessments paid by all residents of Sun City Hilton Head, which cover the cost of operating, repairing and replacing the many community amenities. Residents can learn more about association assessments through information provided by the Finance Committee and the Director of Finance.

### Neighborhood Restricted Reserve Assessment The funds in this Assessment are restricted as to their use, both by Community Governing Documents and by generally accepted accounting principles. The use of these funds is limited to the cost of replacing, repairing or restoring a reserve component to its original functional condition. In the case of Villas, these funds are restricted to the following: - Painting/staining/sealing as appropriate for the type of exterior on your Villa at or near the end of the existing coating’s life. - Replacement of the roofs at the end of their useful life. - Replacement of the gutters and downspouts when the roofs are replaced in The Aviary, The Preserve, Summerplace Village and Seaford Place because the gutters were part of the original Villa built by the Developer. In the other Neighborhoods, if the Villa owner wants to put on gutters after a re-roofing, it would be at their personal expense.

Estimating both the timeframe and expected cost for these long-term items is done by third-party professionals. The Community Association conducts a Reserve Study for all of its assets every three years, and Villas are included in that study. A separate Reserve Study document is developed for each Villa Neighborhood; it can be found on the Documents Section of your Neighborhood’s website. If you would like help understanding the Reserve Study, you can talk to your Neighborhood Representative or contact the Chair of the Villa and Cottage Subcommittee of the Finance Committee. You can reach the Subcommittee Chair through the Finance Committee Chair. The Annual Budget for contributions to the Reserve account is recommended to the Board of Directors by the Finance Committee based on the information in the Reserve Study. In some cases, an updated study may identify a potential shortfall requiring increases in the Assessment level over several years to catch up.

The funds placed into the Neighborhood Reserve Account are managed by the Association in the same manner that the Reserve Funds for all of the Association’s assets are managed. Specifically, reserve contributions are placed in investment instruments according to the Investment Policy recommended by the Finance Committee and approved by the Board of Directors. The Neighborhood Representative is provided a quarterly account statement that shows both the total value and the specific investment instruments for the Neighborhood. The Reserve Study only provides a financial planning tool. The actual timeframe for making any repair or replacement is dictated by the condition of the items being reserved for. Any decisions to repair/replace will be made by the association management company with input from the involved Neighborhood Representatives, as well as other professionals as appropriate. The Neighborhood Representative will be informed of the planned date for work to be performed.

### Neighborhood Operating Assessment As you will see below, most of the operational spending is in a few major items that are largely outside of the control of the Neighborhood, but there is considerable flexibility in the budget setting process to provide funds for special projects the Neighborhood may want to do. The budget process for Villa Neighborhoods is defined in Board Policy 1204.4, which can be found in the Appendices.

### Operating Budget Process The Finance Department prepares the Neighborhood budget based on the forecasted actual budget for the current year and other known information. This proposed budget is then reviewed with the Neighborhood Representative and interested residents at the Neighborhood Budget Review Meeting. Neighborhood Representatives can recommend changes to budget line items based on their knowledge of neighborhood needs. After the Neighborhood Budget Meeting, the Accounting Department presents the budget to the Finance Committee, which presents it to the Board of Directors at a meeting open to all residents. The Board ultimately approves the budget based on recommendations of the Finance Committee. Additional details of this process can be found in Board Policy 1204.4, Resolution to Establish a Formalized Budget Process for Villa and Cottage Neighborhoods. This policy can be found in the Appendices. The Operating budget cannot be used for social functions.

Each of the seven Villa Neighborhoods provide very similar services; however, differences in neighborhood size, construction, age and location may result in differences in required expenses – and thus in Neighborhood Assessments.

### Budget Details The budget details will vary slightly for each Neighborhood. Your Neighborhood Representative will provide you with specific information. The following notes concerning the budget line items will be helpful in understanding the budget. - **Landscaping Service and Insurance** comprises about 80 percent of the budget, and its expense is fixed for the year. The Landscaping Service is a fixed annual price for the term of the contract. The Insurance amount is a combination of specific and allocated premiums for the VillaNeighborhood’s portion of the insurance policy premiums paid by the Association for all of its covered assets. - **Management Fees** for your Neighborhood are determined annually based upon the estimated expenses incurred by the Association to manage the neighborhoods, and includes people, services,supplies and other expenditures.

- **Operating Reserve/Contingency** is an amount determined by Board Policy 1204.4. Briefly, the Board Policy requires that each Neighborhood have an accumulated Operating Reserve (cash left over at year end) of between 2.5 percent and 10 percent of the total assessment for unexpected contingencies. The Operating Reserve/Contingency line item is used to build up the Operating Reserve to an appropriate level. Having a high Operating Reserve helps to avoid large increases in the Operating Assessment in a year to cover a shortfall from the previous year. To manage the Operating Reserve between the minimum and maximum levels, the Neighborhood Representative may request that it be allowed to accumulate or that an amount be returned to the owners, based on Neighborhood preference. Note that this Operating Reserve is completely distinct and separate from the Restricted Reserve Funds described above for repair or replacement of assets at the end of their useful life.

- **Utilities** line items are for the irrigation of the lawn and landscaping around each Villa and in the Exclusive Common Area of the Villa Neighborhood. - **Termite Bond** covers the premium for a termite bond with a service company for treatment, inspection and remediation of termite problems. See the Maintenance Section for additional details on the Termite Bond. - **Power Washing** covers the power washing of the Villas in your Neighborhood. See the Maintenance Section for additional details on power washing. - **Repair and Maintenance** covers repair and maintenance of the irrigation system that are not covered by the contract with the landscape service company, correction of significant drainage problems, and the maintenance and repair of roofs that are not the responsibility of the owner. This item is budgeted based on the previous year’s spending and any special situations of which the Neighborhood Representatives and the Manager of Managed Neighborhoods are aware.

- **Landscaping** covers any landscape improvements or plant material replacement that is not** covered by the contract with the landscape service company, and may include input from the Neighborhood Representatives. This item is budgeted based on the prior experience and any special situations of which the Neighborhood Representative and the Manager of Managed Neighborhoods are aware. - **Insurance Deductible** covers any possible insurance deductible expense for insured losses. See the Insurance Section for additional details.

- **Bad Debt Expense:** The owners of the Villas are responsible for all expenses of the Neighborhood. However, if there are Villa Owners who are not paying their Neighborhood Assessments, the unpaid Assessments can be treated as bad debt by the Community Association. While the Association will take appropriate action to collect the bad debt, the funds available to pay for Neighborhood Expenses will have a shortfall of the unpaid amount. The Bad Debt Expense line item is an amount to compensate for the possibility of unpaid Assessments.

### Review of Financial Reports Your Neighborhood Representatives will review the monthly financial reports that are prepared by the Accounting Department for review by the Finance Committee. They can get clarification on any items from the Accounting Department. Periodically, your Neighborhood Representatives will provide financial status to you at a meeting or by another method. These reports are posted on the community website for review by residents. You can find them in the Documents section of both your Neighborhood’s website and the Finance Committee’s website. The reports on the Finance Committee page contain information for all Departments and Neighborhoods.

### Frequently Asked Questions about Financial Information 1. **Who is responsible for the money paid for Neighborhood Assessments?** The Association’s Accounting Department keeps track of all monies paid with the oversight of the Finance Committee. Neighborhood Representatives may request meetings with the Director of Finance to review spending items. - 2. **What happens if there is a surplus or a shortfall in my Neighborhood Assessment?** See the section above entitled Operating Reserve/Contingency. - 3 **What happens if the Operating Reserve exceeds 10 percent?** An amount can be refunded to owners, or the Assessments in the following year can be reduced. This decision is made during the Neighborhood Operating Budgeting Process as described above.

## Insurance As required by the Governing Documents, the Community Association purchases property insurance that covers risks of physical loss to your unit as it was originally built. To fully insure your Villa, you should obtain an HO-6 (condominium/renters) insurance policy for both the contents and any improvements/additions made to your Villa, as well as for your personal liability. Improvements would include things like enclosing a lanai, a bathroom or kitchen remodel, upgraded floor and wall coverings, etc. You should also consider a flood policy for your contents and improvements/additions.

### Association-Provided Insurance Villa Neighborhoods consist mainly of attached homes, either duplexes or triplexes, and as such require special insurance provisions to protect all owners within the neighborhood. The Governing Documents require certain types of insurance coverage and require the Board of Directors to exercise prudent business judgment with regard to other types of insurance that may not be common or may be more difficult to obtain. _All insurance provided by the Association only insures your Villa as originally built, including standard_ _floor and wall coverings. Insurable values are determined annually by an independent appraisal firm._ _Insurable value reflects the replacement value of your Villa which is different from market value._ The types of insurance coverage provided by the Community Association include property coverage

The types of insurance coverage provided by the Community Association include property coverage (building unit only) for perils including fire, wind and hail, flood and earthquake. From time to time, the Board may decide that other insurance coverage is necessary to protect the villas and these coverages may change. Each of the policies has deductibles for any insured losses. The deductibles may also change depending upon the options available at the time of renewal. Each year upon renewal, a Certificate of Insurance is provided to you and your lender, if applicable. The certificate serves as evidence of coverage and details the specific coverage and deductibles for the year. A sample of a certificate is included at the end of this section. Of course, the wording in the actual policies is the precise definition of coverage and deductibles. **Deductibles** Refer to your current Certificate of Insurance for the up-to-date information on the deductibles for each policy.

Other than for flood damage, any deductibles for villa neighborhood losses covered under Association provided insurance policies are shared among all Villa Owners as described in Board Policy 0807.3, which can be found in the Appendices. The Flood Policy is a per-building policy, so any loss deductible is shared among the building unit owners. Note that Board Policy 0807.3 replaces deductible allocation information in Board Policy No. 0304.7, and its attachment, Board Policy 0304.7 A. As an example, if an entire building in a neighborhood was to be destroyed by fire and there was a single deductible of $5,000, the $5,000 would be shared among the 635 units in all of the seven Villa Neighborhoods. The Neighborhood budget includes a line item for deductibles. **Reporting an Insured Loss**

The Neighborhood budget includes a line item for deductibles. **Reporting an Insured Loss** If there is a possibility that your Villa has sustained an insured loss covered by an Association-provided policy, you should notify the Manager of Managed Neighborhoods at _managed.neighborhoods@schhca.com or (843) 705-4061, who will submit the loss to the appropriate_ party.

### Villa Owner-Provided Insurance You are encouraged to obtain an HO-6 insurance policy specifically for condominium or apartment residents that cover items not covered by the Association-provided policies. Your insurance agent will be able to give you the precise coverage in your HO-6 policy, but in general your H0-6 policy would cover: - The Villa contents, such as your furniture, clothing, computers, etc. - Any upgrades or additions made to your Villa after it was built. This would include things like an enclosed lanai, a bathroom or kitchen remodel, upgraded floor and wall coverings, etc. - Your personal liability resulting from owning your Villa. Villa owners may not insure the entire structure per the Supplemental Declarations to the CC&Rs for your Neighborhood.

You should also consider purchasing a flood insurance policy available from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) since Sun City is in a coastal area subject to flooding. Your insurance agent can obtain this insurance coverage for you. Just as in the case of the HO-6 policy, your flood policy would only be for your contents and any damage to improvements/additions. Flood coverage for the Villa (building) is provided by the Association and included in your Assessments.

### Frequently Asked Questions about Insurance 1. **If I am not the original owner, how do I know if my Villa has upgrades/additions?** The county records office should have records of all building permits. The Community Standards Department in Palmetto Commons would have records of all approved Modification Requests for external changes. Neighbors may be able to tell you about visible changes that were additions or upgrades inside your Villa from their knowledge of the “as built” components. - 2. **Does Wind and Hail coverage include hurricane, tornado and other high wind damage?** Yes. - 3.**Why do we carry Earthquake Coverage?** Per the Governing Documents, the Board of Directors establishes policy regarding what insurance coverage is provided. Our area is in an earthquake zone. See the Board Policies in the Appendices for the latest information.

## Landscaping While insurance is the highest-cost single line item, Landscaping is your most visible and second highest cost benefit. As described briefly in the Overview of Villa Ownership section, you have a deed for your lot that surrounds your Villa by a few feet, but your use of that space is subject to the Governing Documents. The shrubbery and lawn (landscaping) surrounding your unit sit partially on your property and the remainder on the Exclusive Common Area for your Neighborhood. Your ability to change or enhance your landscaping is covered later in this section, but first, it is helpful to understand the day-to-day landscape maintenance.

### Landscape Maintenance Landscape maintenance is provided to you by the Community Association as directed in the Supplemental Declarations. The cost of the service is included in the Neighborhood Operating Assessment, and the Managed Neighborhoods Office manages delivery of this service. The service is performed by a contracted, professional landscaping company.

### Landscaping Contract Scope of Work The scope of work in the contract with the Landscape Service Company provides for the following: **General landscaping services:** - Turf mowing occurs once a week (weather permitting) during the growing season (approximately April through October), and as needed for the remainder of the year. - Edging around walkways, driveways and plant beds. - Debris removal after cutting and trimming. - Weed removal using mechanical, chemical or manual methods. - Continuous program of horticultural proper shrub and ground cover pruning. - Rejuvenation of plants with hard pruning as necessary. - Pruning low-hanging branches on trees. **Irrigation** All aspects of irrigation systems are maintained, which include adjustments, programming and repair as needed.

- Items financially covered under the contract with the Landscape Service Company include: afterhours emergency calls, backflow troubleshooting, general sprinkler head and lateral line work, non-pressurized lines repair (from valve in), rain sensors, sprinkler heads and nozzles, valve boxes and covers and wiring tracing. - Although the Landscape Service Company will service all of the irrigation system, the following items are not financially covered under the contract and any costs are charged to the Irrigation Line Items in the Neighborhood Operating Budget: backflows, docks/controller and pedestals, pressurized mainline, electrical and mechanical valves. **Horticultural Applications** - Turf fertilization twice a year (spring and fall). - Fungicide and insecticide as needed to control disease, fungus and insects. - Pre-emergent and selective post-emergent herbicide for turf weeds. - Plant material fertilization twice a year (spring and fall).

- Plant material fertilization twice a year (spring and fall). - Ornamental trees (including palm trees), fertilized as needed. **Other** - Uniform pruning-no special requests for pruning (i.e. height, to do/not to do, privacy etc.). See the pruning guide below. - Replacement of dead plant material and turf to occur during certain times of the year relative to environmental conditions. - Pine straw application occurs twice a year (spring and fall).
