#### Governing Documents Sun City is a non-profit corporation with a number of Governing Documents that provide both the legal foundation for ownership within Sun City, as well as the operational foundation for actions taken by the Community Association. In order of their legal precedence, the Governing Documents are listed below. Although a brief description of each document is provided, the official wording can be found in the documents themselves and those documents are the authority on which the management of your neighborhood is based. Except where noted, these documents are viewable by logging into **www.SunCityHiltonHead.org, clicking on “Documents” under the Community Library tile and then** clicking “Governing Documents.” 1. **Recorded Plats and Deeds:** Shows the precise location of each lot and the “Exclusive Common Areas.” It also defines the owner’s and the community’s title to the property.

2. **The Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (CC&Rs):** These are part of your deed to your Villa as it is registered in Beaufort County. These were created at the inception of Sun City and are only rarely modified. They can be only modified by the Developer (PulteGroup). However, the Board of Directors can recommend a change to the Developer. 3. **Supplemental Declarations:** These documents are supplements to the CC&Rs for each individual Villa neighborhood that describe specific responsibilities of the Developer, the Association, and the Villa owners related to each neighborhood. They also describe which lots are included in the Neighborhood. In the Appendices, you will find the Supplemental Declaration for your neighborhood and an Amendment to that Supplement. A Neighborhood may request that the Board consider a specific change to their Supplemental Declaration. 4. **Articles of Incorporation:** This document provides the legal description of the Sun City Hilton

Head Corporation. 5. **Bylaws:** This document defines how Sun City Hilton Head operates. They can be amended by the Developer or by the Board with the agreement of the Developer. 6. **Board Policies:** These are issued by the Board to establish an operating policy for something not covered by the above documents. Between Sun City’s incorporation in 1995 and February 2015, the Board has issued 179 policies. As an example, Policy 1401.1 concerns the cleaning of Villa Gutters that you will read about in the Maintenance Section.

7. **Design Guidelines:** The Design Guidelines were established to maintain the integrity of the architectural and design characteristics of Sun City Hilton Head. They describe what changes are permitted to the exterior of a property for all residences in Sun City, including Houses, Cottages and Villas. There are Design Guidelines that are specific to Villas, and these are provided in the Appendices. The Design Guidelines can be changed by the Board of Directors, and the Modifications Committee can recommend changes to the Board. Any new provisions cannot be applied retroactively. 8. **Community Rules:** These are the operating rules provided by the Board to association management, which implements the rules through operating procedures they create. As an example, there are rules as to how many activity cards an owner may have under various situations. There are no Community Rules specific to owners of Villas, but you must still abide by the Rules as a member of Sun City.

You will see how these documents come into play as you read the remainder of this manual. #### Community Standards Collectively, the Governing Documents described above are referred to as the Community Standards and are administered by the Community Standards Department on behalf of the Community Association. If you wanted to make an exterior modification to your home, you would fill out an application describing what you would like to do along with required documentation and submit it to the Community Standards Department. If your modification request meets the requirements of the Governing Documents, primarily the Design Guidelines in this case, it would be approved by the Modifications Committee and you could proceed. Administering the Community Standards in a consistent way throughout Sun City plays a major role in maintaining the beauty and property values of the community. #### Neighborhood Representative Council

#### Neighborhood Representative Council Sun City has approximately 50 different Neighborhoods, including seven Villa Neighborhoods. The Neighborhood Representative Council (NRC), comprised of representatives from the Neighborhoods, meets monthly as an information conduit back and forth between owners in the Neighborhoods, the Board and the Association. The Neighborhoods are also assigned to a District of the NRC. The seven Villa Neighborhoods comprise District 2. Neighborhood Representatives in District 2 meet monthly or as needed to provide a voice for specific interests of the Villa Neighborhoods.

## Financial Information As covered in the Overview of Villa Ownership, you pay two assessments related to the Villa Neighborhood, namely, the restricted Reserve Assessment and the general Operating Assessment. These are described in detail below. While procedurally the Villa Assessment is paid to the Sun City Community Association, these neighborhood assessments are separate and distinct from the association assessments paid by all residents of Sun City Hilton Head, which cover the cost of operating, repairing and replacing the many community amenities. Residents can learn more about association assessments through information provided by the Finance Committee and the Director of Finance.

### Neighborhood Restricted Reserve Assessment The funds in this Assessment are restricted as to their use, both by Community Governing Documents and by generally accepted accounting principles. The use of these funds is limited to the cost of replacing, repairing or restoring a reserve component to its original functional condition. In the case of Villas, these funds are restricted to the following: - Painting/staining/sealing as appropriate for the type of exterior on your Villa at or near the end of the existing coating’s life. - Replacement of the roofs at the end of their useful life. - Replacement of the gutters and downspouts when the roofs are replaced in The Aviary, The Preserve, Summerplace Village and Seaford Place because the gutters were part of the original Villa built by the Developer. In the other Neighborhoods, if the Villa owner wants to put on gutters after a re-roofing, it would be at their personal expense.

Estimating both the timeframe and expected cost for these long-term items is done by third-party professionals. The Community Association conducts a Reserve Study for all of its assets every three years, and Villas are included in that study. A separate Reserve Study document is developed for each Villa Neighborhood; it can be found on the Documents Section of your Neighborhood’s website. If you would like help understanding the Reserve Study, you can talk to your Neighborhood Representative or contact the Chair of the Villa and Cottage Subcommittee of the Finance Committee. You can reach the Subcommittee Chair through the Finance Committee Chair. The Annual Budget for contributions to the Reserve account is recommended to the Board of Directors by the Finance Committee based on the information in the Reserve Study. In some cases, an updated study may identify a potential shortfall requiring increases in the Assessment level over several years to catch up.

The funds placed into the Neighborhood Reserve Account are managed by the Association in the same manner that the Reserve Funds for all of the Association’s assets are managed. Specifically, reserve contributions are placed in investment instruments according to the Investment Policy recommended by the Finance Committee and approved by the Board of Directors. The Neighborhood Representative is provided a quarterly account statement that shows both the total value and the specific investment instruments for the Neighborhood. The Reserve Study only provides a financial planning tool. The actual timeframe for making any repair or replacement is dictated by the condition of the items being reserved for. Any decisions to repair/replace will be made by the association management company with input from the involved Neighborhood Representatives, as well as other professionals as appropriate. The Neighborhood Representative will be informed of the planned date for work to be performed.

### Neighborhood Operating Assessment As you will see below, most of the operational spending is in a few major items that are largely outside of the control of the Neighborhood, but there is considerable flexibility in the budget setting process to provide funds for special projects the Neighborhood may want to do. The budget process for Villa Neighborhoods is defined in Board Policy 1204.4, which can be found in the Appendices.

### Operating Budget Process The Finance Department prepares the Neighborhood budget based on the forecasted actual budget for the current year and other known information. This proposed budget is then reviewed with the Neighborhood Representative and interested residents at the Neighborhood Budget Review Meeting. Neighborhood Representatives can recommend changes to budget line items based on their knowledge of neighborhood needs. After the Neighborhood Budget Meeting, the Accounting Department presents the budget to the Finance Committee, which presents it to the Board of Directors at a meeting open to all residents. The Board ultimately approves the budget based on recommendations of the Finance Committee. Additional details of this process can be found in Board Policy 1204.4, Resolution to Establish a Formalized Budget Process for Villa and Cottage Neighborhoods. This policy can be found in the Appendices. The Operating budget cannot be used for social functions.

Each of the seven Villa Neighborhoods provide very similar services; however, differences in neighborhood size, construction, age and location may result in differences in required expenses – and thus in Neighborhood Assessments.

### Budget Details The budget details will vary slightly for each Neighborhood. Your Neighborhood Representative will provide you with specific information. The following notes concerning the budget line items will be helpful in understanding the budget. - **Landscaping Service and Insurance** comprises about 80 percent of the budget, and its expense is fixed for the year. The Landscaping Service is a fixed annual price for the term of the contract. The Insurance amount is a combination of specific and allocated premiums for the VillaNeighborhood’s portion of the insurance policy premiums paid by the Association for all of its covered assets. - **Management Fees** for your Neighborhood are determined annually based upon the estimated expenses incurred by the Association to manage the neighborhoods, and includes people, services,supplies and other expenditures.

- **Operating Reserve/Contingency** is an amount determined by Board Policy 1204.4. Briefly, the Board Policy requires that each Neighborhood have an accumulated Operating Reserve (cash left over at year end) of between 2.5 percent and 10 percent of the total assessment for unexpected contingencies. The Operating Reserve/Contingency line item is used to build up the Operating Reserve to an appropriate level. Having a high Operating Reserve helps to avoid large increases in the Operating Assessment in a year to cover a shortfall from the previous year. To manage the Operating Reserve between the minimum and maximum levels, the Neighborhood Representative may request that it be allowed to accumulate or that an amount be returned to the owners, based on Neighborhood preference. Note that this Operating Reserve is completely distinct and separate from the Restricted Reserve Funds described above for repair or replacement of assets at the end of their useful life.

- **Utilities** line items are for the irrigation of the lawn and landscaping around each Villa and in the Exclusive Common Area of the Villa Neighborhood. - **Termite Bond** covers the premium for a termite bond with a service company for treatment, inspection and remediation of termite problems. See the Maintenance Section for additional details on the Termite Bond. - **Power Washing** covers the power washing of the Villas in your Neighborhood. See the Maintenance Section for additional details on power washing. - **Repair and Maintenance** covers repair and maintenance of the irrigation system that are not covered by the contract with the landscape service company, correction of significant drainage problems, and the maintenance and repair of roofs that are not the responsibility of the owner. This item is budgeted based on the previous year’s spending and any special situations of which the Neighborhood Representatives and the Manager of Managed Neighborhoods are aware.

- **Landscaping** covers any landscape improvements or plant material replacement that is not** covered by the contract with the landscape service company, and may include input from the Neighborhood Representatives. This item is budgeted based on the prior experience and any special situations of which the Neighborhood Representative and the Manager of Managed Neighborhoods are aware. - **Insurance Deductible** covers any possible insurance deductible expense for insured losses. See the Insurance Section for additional details.

- **Bad Debt Expense:** The owners of the Villas are responsible for all expenses of the Neighborhood. However, if there are Villa Owners who are not paying their Neighborhood Assessments, the unpaid Assessments can be treated as bad debt by the Community Association. While the Association will take appropriate action to collect the bad debt, the funds available to pay for Neighborhood Expenses will have a shortfall of the unpaid amount. The Bad Debt Expense line item is an amount to compensate for the possibility of unpaid Assessments.

### Review of Financial Reports Your Neighborhood Representatives will review the monthly financial reports that are prepared by the Accounting Department for review by the Finance Committee. They can get clarification on any items from the Accounting Department. Periodically, your Neighborhood Representatives will provide financial status to you at a meeting or by another method. ### Pruning Guides The Landscape Service Company is directed to follow pruning guides, and deviations for individual Villas are not permitted. **General Pruning Guide** The pruning approach is designed to create the healthiest and best flowering shrubs possible. The method used in Sun City Hilton Head Villas is a “heading back’’ technique. Using this technique, plants are not simply sheared at the top or along the outside of the plant. Instead, selective cuts are made by hand, both on the interior and exterior of the plant. This creates a looser form plant with foliage throughout and not just on the outer “shell.” Doing so allows greater sunlight and air penetration, creating more foliage and less fungal and insect issues. This results in a healthier plant than would be the case with the quicker approach of just shearing the outside edge.

Flowering shrubs are pruned at the appropriate times of the year. For instance, to have a great display of azalea blooms in the spring, any major pruning is done before late summer. This prevents removal of developing flower buds that will open the following year. This reduced pruning intensity may produce a less “manicured” appearance for certain parts of the year, but it creates the intensive flowering desired. Shearing with hedge trimmers is only done on very select hedging shrubs. Plantings are always maintained to prevent the plant from coming in contact with a part of the Villa structure or addition.

Pruning heights are determined by plant location and variety. In some cases, plants that mature at greater heights than is appropriate for their location have been planted in front of a window. The contractor does its best to control these plants for functionality of the space, aesthetics of the landscape and health of the plant. Plants around the foundation of homes are pruned to maintain a blend of privacy and visibility. Depending on the home design and window placement, shrubs are maintained to cover from 1/4 to 1/2 the window height in the front and rear of the villa. Plants along the sides of homes are pruned in a similar manner but may be higher to provide screening of utility boxes or additional privacy. **Crape Myrtle Pruning Guide**

of utility boxes or additional privacy. **Crape Myrtle Pruning Guide** Crape Myrtle trees are pruned based on the recommendations of Clemson University Cooperative Extension Service and other horticulture authorities. You can read more about Crape Myrtle pruning at **www.clemson.edu/extension/hgic/plants/landscape/trees/hgic1009.html.** The practice of chopping off the tops of Crape Myrtle trees has become very commonplace. Many people believe it is required in order for them to bloom; others see their neighbors doing it and feel they need to follow suit. The best practice is that Crape Myrtles should be allowed to grow to their mature height and require very little pruning, if any, on a yearly basis.

They do not require heavy pruning to promote flower growth. Pruning should only be done to develop shape and promote good health. Growth coming from the ground or lower part of the trunk is removed. Branches that are rubbing against one another (causing wounds) and growing into the center of the canopy are also removed. Seeds can be left on and will fall off naturally and are a great food source for many native bird species. By following these suggestions, a graceful specimen will develop rather than a gnarled and deformed tree. Correct Pruning Incorrect Pruning The landscape maintenance contractor will prune for health, shape and to prevent any trees touching the sides of homes or from hanging over sidewalks and driveways. reason to determine the budget for any year, then and until such time as a budget shall have been determined as provided herein, the budget in effect for the immediately preceding year shall continue for the current year.

(d) Maximum Increase in Base Assessment. Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the Board may not impose a Base Assessment that is more than 20% greater than the Base Assessment for the immediately preceding fiscal year without a majority vote of a quorum of Neighborhood Representatives, which vote may be at a meeting of the Association or by written ballot. This limitation shall not apply to Neighborhood Assessments, Special Assessments, Benefitted Assessments, or any user or membership fees imposed by the Association.

(e) Reduction in Base Assessment. The Declarant may, but shall not be obligated to, reduce the Base Assessment for any fiscal year by payment of a subsidy (in addition to any amounts paid by Declarant under Section 10.2), which may be either a contribution, an advance against future assessments due from the Declarant, or a loan, in the Declarant’s discretion. Any such subsidy shall be disclosed as a line item in the Common Expense budget. The payment of such subsidy in any year shall not obligate the Declarant to continue payment of such subsidy in future years, unless otherwise provided in a written agreement between the Association and the Declarant. 10.4 Computation of Neighborhood Assessments.

(a) Preparing Neighborhood Budget. At least 30 days before the beginning of each fiscal year, the Board shall prepare a separate budget for each Neighborhood covering the estimated Neighborhood Expenses, if any, expected to be incurred on behalf of such Neighborhood during the coming year. The Board shall be entitled to set such budget only to the extent that (i) this Declaration, any Supplemental Declaration, or the Bylaws specifically authorizes the Board to assess certain costs as a Neighborhood Assessment, or (ii) the Association expects to incur expenses to provide additional services for a Neighborhood. Any Neighborhood may request that additional

income for the Association equal to the total budgeted Common Expenses, including contributions to reserves. In determining the level of assessments, the Board, in its discretion, may consider other sources of funds available to the Association. In addition, the Board shall take into account the number of Lots subject to assessment under Section 10.8 on the first day of the fiscal year for which the budget is prepared and the number of Lots reasonably anticipated to become subject to assessment during the fiscal year.

(a) Preparing Neighborhood Budget. At least 30 days before the beginning of each fiscal year, the Board shall prepare a separate budget for each Neighborhood covering the estimated Neighborhood Expenses, if any, expected to be incurred on behalf of such Neighborhood during the coming year. The Board shall be entitled to set such budget only to the extent that (i) this Declaration, any Supplemental Declaration, or the Bylaws specifically authorizes the Board to assess certain costs as a Neighborhood Assessment, or (ii) the Association expects to incur expenses to provide additional services for a Neighborhood. Any Neighborhood may request that additional services or an increased level of services be provided by the Association, and in such case, any approved additional costs shall be added to such budget. Such budget shall include a reserve contribution establishing a fund for repair and replacement of items maintained as a Neighborhood Expense, if any, within the Neighborhood.

(b) Obligation for Neighborhood Assessments. Neighborhood Expenses shall be levied as a Neighborhood Assessment against all Lots within the benefitted Neighborhood and shall be allocated equally among those Lots. If specified in the Supplemental Declaration applicable to such Neighborhood or if directed by petition signed by a majority of the Owners within the Neighborhood, any portion of the assessment intended for exterior maintenance of Dwelling Units or other structures, insurance on Dwelling Units or other structures, or replacement reserves which pertain to particular structures shall be levied on each of the benefitted Lots in proportion to the benefit received. Such proportion shall be specified in the Supplemental Declaration applicable to such Neighborhood, or if not so specified, shall be approved by a majority of the Owners within the Neighborhood, and Declarant, as long as Declarant owns any property within such Neighborhood.

(c) Effective Date. Neighborhood budgets shall become effective unless disapproved by a majority vote of the Owners of Lots in the Neighborhood for which the Neighborhood budget applies. There shall be no obligation to call a meeting or written ballot for the purpose of considering the Neighborhood budget except on written petition of Owners representing at least 10% of the Class “A” votes in such Neighborhood, which petition must be presented to the Board within 30 days after notice of the Neighborhood Assessments. Notice of Neighborhood Assessment shall be provided to Owners in the Neighborhood in the manner set forth in Section 19.10; and provided, further, the right to disapprove shall apply only to those line items in the Neighborhood budget which are attributable to services requested by the Neighborhood. If the Owners within any Neighborhood disapprove any line item of a Neighborhood budget, the Association shall not be obligated to provide the services anticipated to be funded

budget, the Association shall not be obligated to provide the services anticipated to be funded by such line item of the budget. If the Board fails for any reason to determine the Neighborhood budget for any year, then and until such time as such budget shall have been determined as provided herein, the Neighborhood budget in effect for the immediately preceding year shall continue for the current year.

10.5 Reserve Budget. (a) Preparing Reserve Budget The Board shall prepare, on an annual basis, reserve budgets for both general and Neighborhood purposes which take into account the number and nature of replaceable assets, the expected life of each asset, and the expected repair or replacement cost of each asset. Such reserve budgets may also anticipate making additional capital improvements and purchasing additional capital assets. The Board shall include in the Base Assessments and Neighborhood Assessments reserve contributions in amounts estimated to be sufficient to meet these projected needs, if any. (b) Use of Reserve Funds. The Board may adopt resolutions regarding the expenditure of reserve funds, including policies designating the nature of assets for which reserve funds may be expended. Such policies may differ for general Association purposes and for each Neighborhood.

So long as the Declarant owns any portion of the Properties or has the right to annex property pursuant to Section 9.1, neither the Association nor the Board shall adopt, modify, limit or expand such policies without the Declarant’s prior written consent. 10.6 Special Assessments.

In addition to other authorized assessments, the Association may levy Special Assessments from time to time to cover unbudgeted expenses or expenses in excess of those budgeted. Such Special Assessment may be levied against the entire membership, if for Common Expenses, or against the Lots within any Neighborhood, if for Neighborhood Expenses. Such Special Assessments shall become effective unless (a) disapproved at a meeting of the Owners representing at least a majority of the total Class “A” votes allocated to Lots which will be subject to such Special Assessment, or (b) disapproved by the Declarant, as long as the Declarant owns any portion of the Properties or has the right to annex property pursuant to Section 9.1. There shall be no obligation to call a meeting for the purpose of considering Special Assessments except on written petition of the Neighborhood Representatives as provided for special meetings in the Bylaws, which petition must be presented to the Board within 30

for special meetings in the Bylaws, which petition must be presented to the Board within 30 days after notice of the Special Assessment. Notice of Special Assessment shall be in the manner set forth in Section 19.10. Special Assessments shall be payable in such manner and at such times as determined by the Board and may be payable in installments extending beyond the fiscal year in which the Special Assessment is approved.

10.7 Benefitted Assessments. (a) Specific Lots. The Board may levy Benefitted Assessments against particular Lots for expenses incurred or to be incurred by the Association, as follows: (i) to cover the costs, including overhead and administrative costs, of providing benefits, items, or services to the Lot or occupants thereof upon request of the Owner pursuant to a menu of special services which the Board may from time to time authorize to be offered to Owners (which might include, without limitation, landscape maintenance, caretaker service, etc.), which assessments may be levied in advance of the provision of the requested benefit, item or service as a deposit against charges to be incurred by the Owner; and

(ii) to cover costs incurred in bringing the Lot into compliance with the provisions of the Governing Documents, or costs incurred as a consequence of the conduct of the Owner or occupants of the Lot, their licensees, invitees, or guests. The Board shall give the Lot Owner prior written notice and an opportunity for a hearing before levying a Benefitted Assessment under this subsection; provided that no notice or hearing shall be required (a) if the Board reasonably determines that prompt imposition of the Benefitted Assessment is required in order to avoid or decrease possible injury to persons or damage to property, (b) for any Benefitted Assessment that does not exceed two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) for a single occurrence (or such greater amount as may be expressly approved in writing by the Board), or (c) for any matter identified in Section 17.2 of this Declaration as not constituting a “Claim”.

constituting a “Claim”. (b) Lots Within Specific Neighborhood. The Association may also levy a Benefitted Assessment against the Lots within a Neighborhood to reimburse the Association for costs incurred in bringing the Neighborhood into compliance with the provisions of the Governing Documents, provided the Board gives the Neighborhood Representative from such Neighborhood prior written notice and an opportunity for a hearing before levying any such assessment (but subject to the same exceptions as set forth in subsection 10.7(a)(ii), above). 10.8 Date of Commencement of Assessments.

10.8 Date of Commencement of Assessments. The obligation to pay assessments shall commence as to each Lot on the first day of the month following: (a) the date the Lot is made subject to this Declaration, or (b) the date the Board first determines a budget and levies assessments pursuant to this Article, whichever is later. The first annual Base and Neighborhood Assessments against each Lot shall be adjusted according to the number of months remaining in the fiscal year at the time assessments commence on the Lot. 10.9 Lien for Assessments.

(a) Creation of Lien. Failure to pay any assessments authorized in this Article shall create a lien against the Lot against which they are levied until paid unless otherwise specifically precluded in this Declaration. The lien shall also secure payment of costs of the Association, including any fees, fines, interest at the maximum rate then allowed by law, charges, reasonable attorneys’ fees, filing fees and court costs, and administrative costs. Such lien shall be superior to all other liens, except (i) the liens of all taxes, bonds, assessments, and other levies which by law would be superior, and (ii) the lien or charge of a first Mortgage of record made in good faith and for value, as set forth in Section 10.1(b), above. The Association may enforce such lien, when any assessment or other charge is delinquent, by suit, judgment, and foreclosure. The lien shall be in addition to the right of the Association to pursue a claim against the Owner personally.

(b) Foreclosure. The Association may bid for the Lot at the foreclosure sale and acquire, hold, lease, mortgage, and convey the Lot. While a Lot is owned by the Association following foreclosure: (a) no right to vote shall be exercised on its behalf; (b) no assessment shall be levied on it; and (c) each other Lot shall be charged, in addition to its usual assessment, its equal pro rata share of the assessment that would have been charged such Lot had it not been acquired by the Association. The Association may sue for unpaid Common Expenses and costs without foreclosing or waiving the lien securing the same.

(c) Effect of Transfer or Foreclosure of Mortgage. The sale or transfer of any Lot shall not affect the assessment lien or relieve such Lot from the lien for any subsequent assessments. However, a Mortgagee holding a first Mortgage of record or other purchaser of a Lot who obtains title pursuant to foreclosure of the Mortgage shall not be personally liable for assessments on such Lot due prior to acquisition of title by the Mortgagee. . Such unpaid assessments shall be deemed to be Common Expenses collectible from Owners of all Lots subject to assessment under Section 10.8, including such acquirer, its successors and assigns. 10.10 Failure to Assess.

10.10 Failure to Assess. Failure of the Board to fix assessment amounts or rates or to deliver or mail each Owner an assessment notice shall not be deemed a waiver, modification, or a release of any Owner from the obligation to pay assessments. In such event, each Owner shall continue to pay Base Assessments and Neighborhood Assessments on the same basis as for the last year for which an assessment was made, if any, until a new assessment is made, at which time the Association may retroactively assess any shortfalls in collections. 10.11 Exempt Property. The following property subject to this Declaration shall be exempt from payment of Base Assessments, Neighborhood Assessments, and Special Assessments: (a) all Common Area; (b) all property dedicated to and accepted by any governmental authority or public utility; and

(b) all property dedicated to and accepted by any governmental authority or public utility; and (c) if approved by the Declarant and/or the Association, in their sole discretion, property owned by Persons exempt from income taxes under the Internal Revenue Code or South Carolina law if such property is used for purposes listed in the applicable Internal Revenue Code or South Carolina law provision.

### ARTICLE XI: ARCHITECTURAL AND DESIGN STANDARDS 11.1 General. (a) Compliance with Governing Documents. No improvements, additions or modifications (including, without limitation, staking, clearing, excavation, grading and other site work), exterior alteration of existing improvements (including painting), placement or posting of any object or thing on the exterior of any Lot, Dwelling Unit, other structure or the Common Area (such as, without limitation, signs, antennae, clotheslines, playground equipment, pools, propane tanks, lighting, temporary structures, and artificial vegetation), planting or removal of landscaping materials, or installation or removal of an irrigation system shall take place except in compliance with this Article XI and the Governing Documents.

(b) Exception for Certain Interior Improvements. Any Owner may remodel, paint or redecorate the interior of structures, including the Dwelling Unit, on his or her Lot without approval. However, modifications to the interior of screened porches, patios, and similar portions of a Lot visible from outside the structures on the Lot shall be subject to this Article and approval as set forth below. (c) Exception for Certain Repainting or Rebuilding of Exterior Improvements. No approval shall be required to repaint the exterior of a structure in accordance with the originally approved color scheme or to rebuild in accordance with originally approved plans and specifications. (d) Exception for Declarant and Common Area Improvements. This Article shall not apply to the activities of the Declarant or to improvements to the Common Area by or on behalf of the Association.

(e) Declarant Approval of Amendments to Article. This Article may not be amended without the Declarant’s written consent so long as the Declarant owns any Private Amenity or any land subject to this Declaration or subject to annexation to this Declaration. 11.2 Architectural and Design Review. (a) New Construction. Until 100% of the Properties have been developed and conveyed to Home Owners, the Declarant shall have exclusive authority to administer and enforce architectural controls under this Article and to review and act upon all applications for original construction within the Properties. There shall be no surrender of this right prior to that time except in a written instrument executed by Declarant and recorded in the Register of Deeds of Jasper County or Beaufort County, South Carolina. Upon the expiration or surrender of such right by the Declarant, such authority shall be assigned to the Modifications Committee.

(b) Modifications Committee; Fees, Deposits and Sanctions. (i) Modifications Committee. The Board shall establish a Modifications Committee which shall consist of at least three, but not more than nine, persons who shall be appointed and shall serve at the discretion of the Board. The Modifications Committee shall have jurisdiction over modifications, additions, or alterations made on or to existing structures on Lots or containing Dwelling Units and the adjacent open space. The Declarant, or after the termination of the Class B Control Period, the Board shall have the right to veto any action taken by the Modifications Committee which the Declarant or Board determines, in its sole discretion, to be inconsistent with the Design Guidelines.

(ii) Fees. The Modifications Committee may establish and charge reasonable fees (i) for review of applications pursuant to (b)(i), above, or (ii) to provide reasonable funds to offset possible costs to the Association for failure of an applicant or its agent to perform in accordance with the Design Guidelines or the approved application (such as, without limitation, fees for cleanup of debris created by the work). The Modifications Committee may require such fees to be paid in full prior to review of any application. Such fees may include the costs incurred in having any application reviewed by architects, engineers or other professionals. The Declarant and the Association may employ architects, engineers, or other persons as deemed necessary to perform the review. The Board may include the compensation of such persons in the Association’s annual operating budget as a Common Expense.

(iii) Deposits. The Modifications Committee may require the deposit of reasonable sums to provide funds to offset possible costs to the Association for failure of an applicant or its agent to perform in accordance with the Design Guidelines or the approved application (such as, without limitation, fees for cleanup of debris created by the work). The Modifications Committee may require such fees to be paid in full prior to commencement of the approved work. Any deposits remaining after the completion of the approved work shall be promptly refunded to the applicant or the applicant’s designee. (iv) Fines and Other Sanctions. The Modifications Committee may establish and impose a schedule of monetary fines and other sanctions authorized by Section 4.2 for failure of an applicant to perform in accordance with this Article, the Design Guidelines or the approved application; provided, however, such schedule shall be approved in writing by the Board. 11.3 Guidelines and Procedures.

(a) Design Guidelines. The Declarant shall prepare Design Guidelines which shall apply to all construction activities within the Properties, except as provided in Section 11.1. The Declarant shall have sole and full authority to amend the Design Guidelines as long as it owns any portion of the Properties or has a right to annex any property pursuant to Section 9.1, or until the Declarant assigns this authority to the Association in writing, which assignment shall be revocable by the Declarant until such time as the assignment is set forth in a written instrument executed by Declarant and recorded in the Register of Deeds of Jasper County or Beaufort County, South Carolina. After assignment, the Association, through its Board of Directors, shall have the authority to amend the Design Guidelines. The Design Guidelines may contain general provisions applicable to all of the Properties, as well as specific provisions which vary from one portion of the Properties to another depending upon

well as specific provisions which vary from one portion of the Properties to another depending upon the location, unique characteristics, intended use, the Master Plan, and any other applicable zoning ordinances. The Design Guidelines are intended to provide guidance to Owners regarding matters of particular concern in considering applications hereunder. The Design Guidelines are not the exclusive basis for decisions of the Modifications Committee and compliance with the Design Guidelines does not guarantee approval of any application.

(b) Amendments to Design Guidelines. Any amendments to the Design Guidelines shall apply to construction and modifications commenced after the date of such amendment only and shall not apply to construction or modifications previously approved if such approved construction or modification has commenced. After the Declarant no longer has authority to amend the Design Guidelines as set forth in subsection (a), there shall be no limitation on the scope of amendments to the Design Guidelines. The Declarant or, upon assignment, the Association, through its Board of Directors, is expressly authorized to amend the Design Guidelines to remove requirements previously imposed or otherwise to make the Design Guidelines less restrictive.

(c) Availability of Design Guidelines. The Association shall make the Design Guidelines available to Owners and builders who seek to engage in development or construction within the Properties and all such Persons shall conduct their activities in accordance with such Design Guidelines. In the Declarant’s discretion, such Design Guidelines may be recorded in the Register of Deeds, in which event the recorded version, as it may unilaterally be amended from time to time, shall control in the event of any dispute as to which version of the Design Guidelines was in effect at any particular time. (d) Variances from Design Guidelines. All structures and improvements constructed upon a Lot shall be constructed in strict compliance with the Design Guidelines in effect at the time the plans for such improvements are submitted to and approved by the Modifications Committee unless the Modifications Committee has granted a variance in writing pursuant to Section 11.6.

So long as the Modifications Committee has acted in good faith, its findings and conclusions with respect to appropriateness of, applicability of or compliance with the Design Guidelines and this Declaration shall be final. 11.4 Review of Plans and Specifications. (a) Mandatory Review of Plans. No activities within the scope of Section 11.1 shall commence on any Lot until an application for approval of the proposed work has been submitted to and approved by the Modifications Committee. Such application shall be in the form required by the Modifications Committee and shall include plans and specifications (“Plans”) showing site layout, structural design, exterior elevations, exterior materials and colors, signs, landscaping, drainage, lighting, irrigation, utility facilities layout and screening therefor and other features of proposed construction, as applicable. The Design Guidelines shall set forth the procedure and any additional information for submission of the Plans.

(b) Review Considerations. In reviewing each submission, the Modifications Committee may consider quality of workmanship and design, visual and environmental impact, ecological compatibility, natural platforms and finish grade elevation, harmony of external design with surrounding structures and environment, and location in relation to surrounding structures and plant life. The Modifications Committee may require relocation of native plants within the construction site or the installation of an irrigation system for the landscaping including the natural plant life on the Lot as a condition of approval of any submission.

(c) Time for Review. The Reviewing Body shall, within the period specified in the Design Guidelines, advise, in writing, the party submitting the Plans, at the address specified by such party at the time of submission or such revised address as is subsequently provided in writing to the Modifications Committee (the “Current Address”) of (i) the approval of the submitted Plans, or (ii) if not approved, the portions of disapproved Plans which are deemed by the Modifications Committee to be inconsistent or not in conformity with this Declaration and/or the Design Guidelines, with a brief summary of the reason for such finding (which may include the need for more information). If the Modifications Committee fails to provide such written notice within the period specified in the Design Guidelines, approval of the Plans shall be deemed to have been given.

(d) Notice to Applicant. Notice to the party submitting the Plans required by (c), above, shall be deemed to have been given when (i) such notice, addressed to the address of party submitting the Plans as set forth on the application, is deposited, postage prepaid, with the U.S. Postal Service and sent by United States First Class mail, in which event delivery shall be deemed to occur three (3) days after the date of deposit with the U.S. Postal Service; or (ii) at the time of delivery to the submitting party at the address specified, or hand delivery to the submitting party or the agent of the submitting party at the office of the Modifications Committee.

(e) Start and Completion of Approved Construction. If construction does not commence on a project for which Plans have been approved within 120 days of the date shown on the notice of such approval, such approval shall be deemed withdrawn, and it shall be necessary for the Owner to resubmit the Plans to the Modifications Committee for reconsideration; provided, however, that the Modifications Committee may, in its sole discretion, grant a written extension of the time for commencement of construction. If construction is not completed on a project for which plans have been approved within the period set forth in the Design Guidelines or in the approval, such approval shall be deemed withdrawn, and such incomplete construction shall be deemed to be in violation of this Article. 11.5 No Waiver of Future Approvals.

11.5 No Waiver of Future Approvals. Each Owner acknowledges that the members of the Modifications Committee will change from time to time and that interpretation, application and enforcement of the Design Guidelines may vary accordingly. Approval of proposals, plans and specifications, or drawings for any work done or proposed, or in connection with any other matter requiring approval, shall not be deemed to constitute a waiver of the right to withhold approval as to any similar proposals, plans and specifications, drawings, or other matters subsequently or additionally submitted for approval. 11.6 Variance.

11.6 Variance. The Modifications Committee may authorize variances in writing from its guidelines and procedures, but only: (a) in accordance with duly adopted rules and regulations, (b) when unique circumstances dictate, such as, without limitation, unusual topography, natural obstructions, hardship or aesthetic or environmental considerations require, and (c) when construction in accordance with the variance would be consistent with the purposes of the Declaration and compatible with existing and anticipated uses of adjoining properties. Inability to obtain, or the terms of, any governmental approval, or the terms of any financing shall not be considered a hardship warranting a variance. Notwithstanding the above, the Modifications Committee may not authorize variances without the written consent of the Declarant, as long as the Declarant owns any portion of the Properties or has a right to annex any property pursuant to Section 9.1.

11.7 Limitation of Liability for Application Decisions. Review and approval of any application pursuant to this Article is made on the basis of aesthetic considerations only and neither the Declarant, the Association, the Board, nor the Modifications Committee shall bear any responsibility for ensuring the structural integrity or soundness of approved construction or modifications, or for ensuring compliance with building codes and other governmental requirements. Neither the Declarant, the Association, the Board, nor the Modifications Committee, nor any member, director, officer, or authorized agent of any of the foregoing shall be held liable for any injury, damages, or loss arising out of the manner or quality of approved construction on or modifications to any Lot. In all matters, the foregoing shall be defended and indemnified by the Association as provided in this Declaration or the Bylaws. 11.8 Enforcement; Completion; Agents of Owner Enforcement.

Any construction, alteration or other work done in violation of this Article or the Design Guidelines shall be deemed to be nonconforming. Upon written request from the Declarant, the Modifications Committee, or the Board, Owners shall, at their own cost and expense and within such reasonable time frame as set forth in such written notice, cure such nonconformance to the satisfaction of the requester or promptly restore the property, Lot and/or Dwelling Unit to substantially the same condition as existed prior to the nonconforming work. Should an Owner fail to remove and restore as required, the Declarant, the Association or its designees shall have the right to enter the property, remove the violation, and restore the property to substantially the same condition as previously existed. All costs of the Association, including any fees, fines, interest at the maximum rate then allowed by law, charges, reasonable attorneys’ fees, filing fees and court costs, and administrative costs, may

charges, reasonable attorneys’ fees, filing fees and court costs, and administrative costs, may be assessed against the benefitted Lot and collected as a Benefitted Assessment unless otherwise prohibited in this Declaration.

(b) Completion Required. All approvals granted hereunder shall be deemed conditioned upon completion of all elements of the approved work and all work previously approved with respect to the same Lot, unless approval to modify any application has been obtained. In the event that any Person fails to commence and diligently pursue to completion all approved work, the Declarant or the Association shall, unless otherwise prohibited in this Declaration, be authorized, after notice to the Owner of the Lot and an opportunity to be heard in accordance with the Bylaws, to enter upon the Lot and remove or complete any incomplete work and to assess all costs incurred against the Lot and the Owner thereof as a Benefitted Assessment. (c) Contractor As Agent of Owner. For the purposes of this Article, all acts by any contractor, subcontractor, agent, employee, or invitee of an Owner shall be deemed as an act done

by or on behalf of such Owner. Any contractor, subcontractor, agent, employee, or other invitee of an Owner who fails to comply with the terms and provisions of this Article and the Design Guidelines may be excluded from the Properties, subject to the notice and hearing procedures contained in the Bylaws. In such event, neither the Declarant, the Association, its officers, or directors shall be held liable to any Person for exercising the rights granted by this paragraph. (d) Other Remedies. In addition to the foregoing, the Association and the Declarant shall have the authority and standing to pursue all legal and equitable remedies available to enforce the provisions of this Article.

# Boat/RV Facility Rules and Regulations The Sun City Hilton Head Boat/RV Facility is a Community Association-owned amenity provided to eligible community residents. This amenity is intended to be utilized as a parking area, not to be used as a storage facility. Any infraction of the Community Association’s Governing Documents, including these rules and regulations, may result in fines, loss of parking and campsite privileges, loss of community privileges, and other enforcement actions that are warranted, including units being towed from the facility. The Community Association will levy all fines per the Community Association Schedule of Fees and Community Rules, and any other enforcement actions that are warranted as stated in the Schedule of Fees and Community Rules. The term “unit” will include all boats, RVs (all classes and sizes), all travel trailers, specialty hobby trailers, personal-use utility trailers, vehicle trailers, motorcycle trailers, and all other trailers.
These rules and regulations are subject to change by the Sun City Hilton Head Board of Directors as deemed appropriate.

## GENERAL RULES, POLICIES AND PROCEDURES 1. A fee of $100 payable to the Community Association is required at the time of application. A copy of a valid registration (if applicable) and current insurance must be submitted with the application. The deposit is non-refundable if made after January 2021. Deposits made before January 2021 will be refunded if/when the resident removes their unit from the Boat/RV Facility and notifies the Lot Manager of termination by filling out a form and submitting it.

2. An annual site fee will be charged on the January statement to the resident’s Community Association account for their unit site(s). This charge is based on the resident’s unit type and unit size. Proof of unit registration, if applicable, and unit valid insurance will be requested annually. Refer to the Community Association Schedule of Fees and Community Rules for the current fee amount. A prorated amount of the fee will be refunded when the resident removes their unit from the Boat/RV Facility and notifies the Community Association Lot Manager of termination of agreement. 3. Only one unit is permitted in each site, with the exception of a tow dolly (space permitting) parked behind a RV with the Lot Manager’s approval.

4. No units for resident contractors or resident commercial/business use are permitted to have unit sites in the facility. Signage, including but not limited to, for sale, contractors, businesses or advertising of any kind, is not allowed to be posted on the units or in the Boat/RV Facility. Signage as to rules, events and information for the users of the sites is allowed but must be approved by the Lot Manager before posting. 5. Sheds, storage containers, or any materials, etc. are not permitted on unit sites with the exception of boat storage locker/containers for boat covers/equipment. 6. Units must be “road ready” at all times. The Community Association defines “road ready” as follows: - Current valid registration (if applicable) and current valid insurance assigned to the resident owner of the unit(s) - Tires are inflated - Good condition (both operational and in clean appearance) as determined by Lot Manager

- Good condition (both operational and in clean appearance) as determined by Lot Manager - Units and/or property in disrepair or non-compliant with the rules set forth in this document will not be permitted to park in the facility. Failure to comply or correct deficiencies within 15 days after written notification may result in a fine and loss of facility privileges. If corrective action is not made within 45 days after written notification, the unit and/or property may be towed from the Boat/RV Facility at the owner’s expense, including moving, towing and storage fees. 7. Each unit must be assigned to a single resident bearer of liability. 8. Parking of additional units on a temporary basis is limited to the resident’s site space dimensions and the Lot Manager’s pre-approval. 9. Open utility trailers shall be empty of cargo, except for a spare tire.

9. Open utility trailers shall be empty of cargo, except for a spare tire. 10. Assigned sites are not transferrable between units or residents. Do not park your unit on another site without notifying the Lot Manager. The Lot Manager has the authority to reassign or change an assigned site as needed. 11. A change of a unit is a new unit, for the purpose of a site assignment and decals. Communication to the Lot Manager of a change in unit is required. This may result in the “new” unit being assigned to a different site. 12. Driving is only permitted through the aisles. Do not enter or drive through unoccupied sites. The speed limit within the facility is 10 mph for safety and to keep dust to a minimum.

13. Unit covers shall be constructed to fit your type of unit and constructed of sturdy materials with all corners and edges securely tied down. Drop cloths, tarps and any cover made of plastic, including shrink wrap, are not permitted. Ripped or torn covers are not permitted. Covers should be clean, not showing mold or dirt, and should be stored when not in use. Any exceptions will need the approval of the Lot Manager. 14. Only gray/black water shall be deposited in the dump station holding tanks. No chemicals, fuels,cleaning solutions or pollutants should be deposited into the dump station tanks. Water and the hose at the dump station is “non potable.”

15. The wash bay is to be used for washing and rinsing your boat or RV. Washing/rinsing of any personal vehicles not stored in the Boat/RV Facility is prohibited. Flushing of boat motors is allowed. RV units have priority until 2 p.m.; boats have priority after 2 p.m. Priority does not mean “not allowed” after a certain time. It means if the station is occupied, the person can finish what they are doing, and the priority would then be next, before any others enter the station. No chemicals, fuels, or pollutants should be deposited into the drain or on the ground. Hoses at wash station are “non potable.”

16. Electrical outlets are for the use of small tools and for the charging of batteries. Air conditioners/heaters shall not be operated using this power unless preparing for a trip. Units should not be plugged in all the time, exception being the Class A diesel engine units that require more power. Other smaller diesels do not require full time electrical charging. Trickle chargers at 14 gauge wire are allowed. Only a 12 gauge or larger extension cord, no longer than 50 feet are to be used. In preparation of a unit for a trip, the unit may be plugged in, 30 amps, for running the refrigerator and A/C or heat no longer than 48 hours. The Lot Manager has the authority to unplug a unit that is plugged in that is in violation of this rule. The Lot Manager will notify the site holder of the violation to the rule by email before unplugging the unit. No response to the Lot Manager’s email notice could result in the unit being unplugged.

Fines or termination of the site agreement could occur as a result of not complying with these rules/ guidelines. A reduced nightly campsite rate of $15 is available for trip preparation or to complete significant repairs or maintenance. Occupancy of the unit is not allowed. Maximum of four nights or longer based on availability and prior approval by the Boat and RV Yard Committee. Contact campsite reservations at (843) 705-3433 to reserve a campsite. 17. This facility is not equipped with trash receptacles or dumpsters. Trash/debris of any kind shall not be left on the premises. Failure to comply could result in sanctions levied against the violators. It is the resident’s responsibility to keep their site clean and free of debris.

18. Due to stringent storm water quality guidelines enforced by South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control (DHEC), repairs to a unit, such as replacing hydraulic brakes, oil changes, repairs to drive trains or motors, etc., are not permitted. No work is to be done on units where liquid (other than drinking water) could be discharged onto the ground. While performing authorized repairs, do not leave anything on the ground unattended or overnight. Should liquids (other than drinking water) be drained or spilled onto the ground, the resident should notify the Lot Manager. Residents may be assessed for any and all costs associated with the cleanup, including fines levied by any government agency as a result of contamination of the site.

19. Should you be unable to safely repair your unit in its parking site, you may temporarily move it to another location with the following conditions. If you only require electrical power, then move to site F-0 (temporary location, 48-hour limit). If you require water and/or sewer service, or extra space then call the campground reservation phone (843) 705-3433, and state that you are in need of a campsite for maintenance. This site is free until sunset. If your unit stays overnight in a campsite, you must contact campsite reservation to gain site permission and to pay the nightly Maintenance fee NO overnight occupancy allowed. If you are going to stay overnight in the unit, campsite reservations must be notified and an appropriate campsite fee is charged.

A reduced nightly campsite rate of $15 is available for trip preparation or to complete significant repairs or maintenance. Occupancy of the unit is not allowed. Maximum of four nights or longer based on availability and prior approval by the Boat and RV Yard Committee. Contact campsite reservations at (843) 705-3433 to reserve a campsite. 20. For safety reasons, steps and/or slide outs are not permitted to be extended overnight. Occupancy of your unit overnight in your assigned site is not allowed. 21. If a resident with a unit parked in the Boat/RV Facility sells their house prior to the completion of a new house being built or resale/purchase (i.e., becoming a non-resident), the resident may continue to park said unit in the facility. The resident will need to provide proof of a sales contract that is in force and rental site fees for the unit must be paid to cover the time period.

22. Residents are permitted to take their units to their homes per the Sun City Hilton Head Community Association’s Schedule of Fees and Community Rules. 23. If a resident plans to remove their unit for more than six consecutive months, but less than nine months, they must send a note to the Lot Manager stating their departure and return date in order to retain the space.

## UNIT TYPES AND CONDITIONS 1. Recreational Vehicles (RV) are defined as a motorized vehicle or trailer designed and manufactured with temporary living quarters for recreational camping travel or seasonal use. Units that measure more than 102 inches at their widest point will not be permitted. SUVs and vans that do not have temporary living quarters are not permitted for sites in the facility. 2. Specialty hobby trailers and utility trailers are defined as an open or closed type trailer, which has a single or double axel and does not include manufactured installed living quarters. These trailers have either a drop-down ramp or detachable ramps for entry/removal of classic/antique vehicles, motorcycles, four-wheel all-terrain vehicles (ATVs) or two-wheel off-road motor bikes as well as used for general storage or transportation.

3. Specialty hobby trailers and personal-use utility trailers are authorized to park in the Boat/RV Facility when space is available on a first-come, first-served basis. These vehicles must be equipped with their own wheels. 4. Boats shall be on trailers during the majority of the year. Empty boat trailers are not permitted, except during summer boating season, beginning May 1 and ending September 30. If a resident plans a longer time they must send a note to the Lot Manager as outlined in Rule 23 above. 5. Non-self-propelled units, (i.e. sail boats, boats, canoes, kayaks, etc.) are not permitted in the facility.

6. RVs, travel trailers and boats have priority if the facility is full and spaces are needed. Specialty hobby units and personal-use utility units will be required to vacate the facility to allow for RV and boat parking based on a last in, first out and square foot requirement. The original date of parking will be based on Community Association facility files. The order for removal will be: Utility units first and specialty hobby units second. When an occurrence arises for removal, names of all owners parked in the facility will be grouped (i.e., personal-use utility units as a group and specialty hobby units as another group); the last in, first out rule will apply per group according to the priority listed above beginning with utility units. The process will be conducted by the Community Association Management and the Lot Manager. The owners will have 15 days to vacate the facility after receiving written notification from the Community Association.

7. Members with boats may place a storage box behind their boat (space permitting). All storage boxes for the boats must be a neutral color. All storage boxes must be approved by the Lot Manager. All material and equipment shall be kept inside the boat box. 8. A limit of one type of each unit per household will be allowed into the facility: one boat, one RV/travel trailer, one specialty hobby trailer, one personal-use trailer.

## SAFETY, SECURITY AND INFORMATION The Boat/RV Facility is unmanned. Video surveillance cameras are installed on the property for safety and security. 1. Located near the entrance to the wash station is an emergency phone and an Automated Emergency Defibrillator (AED), with voice activation and directions on how to use attached. Fire extinguishers are on most light poles throughout the facility. 2. To the right as you enter the facility is the Boat/RV bulletin board with a site listing of names and phone numbers, in addition to important information for the facility users. 3. Do not allow anyone to use your authorized activity card to gain access to the facility. The penalty for violating this rule is as follows: - First offense: A fine per the Community Association Schedule of Fees and Community Rules. - Second offense: A fine plus a 12-month suspension of parking and campsite privileges.

- Second offense: A fine plus a 12-month suspension of parking and campsite privileges. - Third offense: After written notice has been received, the resident will have 15 days to remove all of their units. Failure to remove the units in a timely manner will result in towing the units from the facility at the owner’s expense. 4. Entry is only permitted by an authorized activity card. When entering the facility, stop after you are through the gate and wait until the gate is completely closed before proceeding into the facility. Once you have passed through the gate, you must stop and wait for the gate to completely close behind you. Everyone entering the facility must scan their authorized activity card and follow the proper procedures. **Failure to comply with entry and exit gate closure procedures may result in the same penalties as delineated in line item 3 above.**

5. Any issues with opening or closing of the gate should be reported to Security at the phone number on the gate. 6. Exit from the facility is by an authorized activity card. When exiting the facility, stop after you are through the gate, wait until the gate is fully closed before proceeding. When there is more than one vehicle leaving the facility at the same time, the first vehicle will scan their authorized activity card and pass through the gate, the other vehicles will follow the first vehicle through the gate scanning their authorized activity card and proceeding to exit. The last vehicle will stop after going through the gate and wait for the gate to fully close before proceeding. **Failure to comply with entry and exit gate closure procedures may result in the same penalties as delineated in line item 3 above.**

7. An authorized resident is a Sun City resident who is renting a site in the facility who wishes to bring an unauthorized vehicle (guest or i.e. repair or maintenance person) into the facility must follow this procedure: - Scan your authorized activity card and enter the facility. - Have your guest follow you through the gate. - The same procedure is followed upon exit from the facility. 8. Guests must be accompanied by owners at all times when inside the facility. Owners are responsible for their guest’s actions and behavior. This includes all service providers working on units. Anyone who causes damage to any of the facilities or equipment or units will be billed for the cost of the repairs and may be assessed an appropriate fine. Anyone found to damage another unit in the facility and not report it to the owner and the Lot Manager is subject to removal from the facility and loss of their site or sites.

9. Loss of parking privileges may result in suspension from the facility for one year. A suspended resident cannot apply for another parking space for one year from the date of suspension. The purpose of the Sun City Hilton Head Boat/RV Facility is to enhance Sun City Hilton Head residents’ active lifestyle. Residents may park their boats, RVs and trailers in the facility with easy access to their units for trips and outings. Long-term storage non-use is not allowed. This is an active use facility; it is not a storage facility for unused units as defined by the rules and regulations stated in this document.

# SCHH Pickleball Club Lottery Program – REV. 0716b2024 ## SCHH Pickleball Club Lottery Rules Please read the following information carefully, as some rules have changed for this upcoming session. It’s important for the players AND the Group Leaders to understand these rules. **The most significant changes have been bolded throughout this document.** ---

### PLAYER INFORMATION 1. **Players may participate in two groups**: - If you choose to play in only one group, that group will be entered into **Lottery Draw A**. - If you choose to play in a second group, that group will be entered into **Lottery Draw B**. - **Important**: Your name can only be entered once in Lottery Draw A and once in Lottery Draw B. 2. **Your Group(s) may play up to three (3) times a week.** 3. **Group rosters require the following number of players**: - 1 hour on 1 court – **4 players** - 1 hour on 2 courts – **8 players** - 2 hours on 1 court – **4 players** - 2 hours on 2 courts – **8 players** ---

### SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR GROUP LEADERS 1. The **Group Leader (GL)** must verify all members of their group are: - SCHH Pickleball Club members. - Registered with the Chelsea Booking System. 2. The GL must be listed as the **first member** of the group roster. 3. The GL must include their **contact email and phone number**. 4. **All players listed in a group must be actual players**: - Spouse, neighbor, or friend from the same household **cannot fill rosters unless they are actually playing.** 5. Before submitting the registration form: - Ensure players in Lottery Draw A rosters are unique (no shared names with another roster). - Similarly, players in Lottery Draw B rosters must also be unique. 6. If a player drops out during the lottery term: - The **Group Leader (GL)** is responsible for replacing the player and updating the reservation with the new player’s name. ---

### REGISTRATION PROCESS - The electronic registration link will be emailed to **all current PB Club members**. - Only **Group Leaders (GL)** are required to submit the registration. - Failure to meet requirements results in: 1. GL being notified of the error via email. 2. GL must edit the registration by the deadline. 3. The group registration will move to the bottom of **Round 1 in Lottery Draw A** or the bottom of **Round 4 in Lottery Draw B**. ---

### LOTTERY DRAW PROCEDURE 1. **Randomization**: - Groups are randomized, and numbers are assigned to each group for each day of play. - Example: Playing one day a week = one number; two days a week = two numbers; three days a week = three numbers. 2. **Draw Rounds**: - The draw consists of **6 rounds**: - **Lottery Draw A**: Rounds 1 through 3. - **Lottery Draw B**: Rounds 4 through 6. 3. On **Lottery Day**: - The GL or one of their group members **must attend**. 4. Reminder: - All rosters in Lottery Draw A must be unique. - All rosters in Lottery Draw B must also be unique. ---

### MISCELLANEOUS NOTES 1. **PickleTennis** permanent court reservations will occur in **Draw C**. 2. Changes or adjustments to the Lottery Program are at the discretion of the **Pickleball Club Board**. 3. **Registration Window**: - Opens: **August 7, 2024** - Closes: **September 7, 2024, at 4:00 PM** - **No registrations will be accepted after the deadline.**

## Cards & Games Clubs - Bid Whist Club - Canasta Club - Contract Bridge Club - Cribbage Club - Dominoes Club - Euchre Club - Gin Rummy Club - Hearts Club - Mah Jongg - Pinochle Club - Rummikub-Qwirkle

### Bid Whist Club A Fun and Easy Card Game to Play. Bid Whist is a variant, played in the United States, of the classic card game, whist. As indicated by the name, bid whist adds a bidding element to the game that is not present in classic whist. It is generally accepted that the game of bridge came from the game of whist.

### Canasta Club The Canasta Club meets Thursdays and Sundays from 12:30 to 4 PM in the Yemassee Craft Center Card Room across from Purrysburg Fitness Center. We welcome all residents who play any form of Canasta. If you have a home game, bring your team and join the fun. There are many variations of Canasta played by our members. We offer lessons to members for Super Samba on the 2nd Thursday of every month.

### Contract Bridge Club All games are played at the Yemassee Craft Center. Tuesday Game 12:45 pm, Wednesday Game 8:30 am., and Thursday Game 8:30 am. are open to all using Chicago scoring. Friday partners, Chicago scoring 6:30 pm.
### Cribbage Club The Cribbage club encourages players to test their skills in a friendly atmosphere of competition each week.
### Dominoes Club Welcome! We play Mexican Train Dominoes. Don't know how to play? No problem. Join us any Monday and we will teach you.
### Euchre Club We invite anyone who plays the game or wants to learn to come join this fun group of people.
### Gin Rummy Club Brighten your Tuesday evening by spending the evening with the Gin Rummy Club enjoying some good company, conversation and a fun game of cards.
### Hearts Club Join us in playing one of the great card games.
### Mah Jongg Open to all levels of play.

### Okatie Creek Duplicate Bridge Club We welcome all bridge players interested in a friendly competitive bridge game. We are a sanctioned ACBL club awarding Master Points. Lessons are available for beginners, intermediate and advanced players. We play on Mondays 1–4:15 p.m., Tuesdays 9 a.m.–12:15 p.m. (2 games per month are team games) and Saturdays 9 a.m.–12:15 p.m. Hands are pre-dealt. Results and analysis of hands played are posted on the website following games. If you need a partner, check out our website. Check the webpage listed above for details about lessons and special events.

### Pinochle Club We play double deck for Move-Up and Non Move-Up games (Move-Up Games consist of changing partners and winners advance to the next table... Non Move-up consists of staying on one table and playing with your same group throughout the night). Move-up game begins at 6 p.m.
### Rummikub-Qwirkle Two different fun, competitive and social games open to all Sun City residents.
